rows.output: Czeisler's research found that the human body has a natural clock that regulates our sleep-wake cycle, which is controlled by the release of melatonin, a hormone that affects our sleep-wake cycle. rows.reference: Prof Czeisler recommended that students should consider setting an alarm for when to go to bed, as well as for when to wake, and be aware of the harmful effects of 'blue light' emitted by electronic screens and LED lighting, which can throw your circadian rhythm out of kilter, leading to problems falling asleep.

rows.output: Rangers won their first trophy in five years as they defeated Dolly Menga's team, Livingston, 1-0, with Steven Gerrard scoring the only goal.
rows.reference: Rangers suffered another bout of away-day blues as Dolly Menga's strike consigned Steven Gerrard's disjointed side to a 1-0 defeat at Livingston.

rows.source: Ikọ̀ ti Ibrox náà ńwá láti ṣàkọsílẹ̀ ìborí àkọ́kọ́ wọn lójú ọ̀nà láti ìgbà ìborí 4-1 tíwọ́n ní ni St Johnstone ninu oṣù Ẹrẹ́ná, ṣùgbọ́n ikọ̀ ti Gary Holt ṣe wọ́nní ìpalára ìjìyà ẹlẹ́ẹ̀kejì tí Gerrard yóò ní ninu àwọn ìdíje méjìdínlógún gẹ́gẹ́bí olùṣàkóso láti fi àwọn kókó mẹ́jọ ti ikọ̀ rẹ̀ sílẹ̀ láìní àfojúsùn Hearts ikọ̀ Ladbrokes tíwọ́n jẹ́ adarí Líìgí Àkọ́kọ́.
rows.output: Ibrox's title race is now a two-horse race, with Rangers looking to win the title for the first time since 2011 after their 4-1 victory over St Johnstone in the Scottish Premiership on Sunday, while Hearts, who were runners-up last season, are now 13 points behind.
rows.reference: The Ibrox side were looking to record their first win on the road since February's 4-1 triumph at St Johnstone, but Gary Holt's team inflicted just Gerrard's second defeat in 18 games as manager to leave his side eight points adrift of runaway Ladbrokes Premiership leaders Hearts.

rows.output: Gerrard scored in the break as he poked the ball past Coulibaly after Kent's cross was deflected into his path. He then turned provider, setting up Morelos for the second goal, Kelly's first of the season, before the striker darted into space to score.
rows.reference: Gerrard acted at the break as he swapped Coulibaly for Ryan Kent and the switch almost provided an immediate impact as the winger slotted in Morelos but the impressive Kelly raced from his line to block.

rows.output: This Sunday morning, we bring you a special report from the 1882 World's Fair in Chicago: In the year 1882, on the 22nd of September, at 10:16 in the morning, the first electric light was turned on in the United States. It was brought to life by the hands of NKA... the electric light was brought to life by the hands of the German inventor Johannes Wilhelm "Hans" Geiger.
rows.reference: And now a page from our "Sunday Morning" Almanac: September 30, 1882, 136 years ago today, and COUNTING ... the day the future physicist Johannes Wilhelm "Hans" Geiger was born in Germany.

rows.source: Geiger ṣàgbékalẹ̀ ọgbọ́n-àtiṣenǹkan fún dídámọ̀ àti ṣíṣe òdiwọ̀n àwọn ìtújáde tíwọn pè ni oníṣẹ́rédíò, àgbélẹ̀rọ eyiti o pàpà yọrísì ẹ̀rọ náà tíwọ́n mọ̀ sí Geiger Counter.
rows.output: Geiger counter is a device that measures the level of radiation in the environment. It is used to detect and measure the amount of radiation that is present in the air, water, or other materials. The device is named after its inventor, Hans Geiger, who developed it in the 1920s.
rows.reference: Geiger developed a method for detecting and measuring radioactivity, an invention that eventually led to the device known as the Geiger Counter.

rows.source: Òpómúléró kan ti ìmọ̀ sáyẹ́ǹsì láti ìgbà náà, Olóǹkà Geiger di òpó fún àṣà pop bákannáà, bótirí ninu àwòrán sinnimá ọdún 1950 ''Àwọn Agogo ti Colorado,'' eyiti àwọn onímọ̀ sáyẹ́nsì tíwọn fúnníṣe àgbàṣe wọ̀nyẹn tí a kò lérò ROY Rogers àti Dale Evans ti kópa:
rows.output: A group of scientists from the Geiger Institute conducted a study in the 1950s, which was also the subject of a 1953 film, "The Colorado City," starring the famous cowboy duo Roy Rogers and Dale Evans.
rows.reference: A mainstay of science ever since, the Geiger Counter became a pop culture mainstay as well, as in the 1950 movie "Bells of Coronado," starring those seemingly unlikely cowpoke scientists Roy Rogers and Dale Evans:

rows.output: The method of treatment is the administration of trastuzumab, a monoclonal antibody against the HER2 receptor, which is overexpressed in some breast cancer cells. This drug targets the HER2 receptor and helps to kill the cancer cells.
rows.reference: The method involves extracting immune cells from a patient, altering them in the laboratory so they can "see" a protein common to many cancers called HER2, and then reinjecting the cells.

rows.source: HER2 ''ńwakọ̀ ìdàgbàsókè ti ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ onírúurú jẹjẹrẹ,'' ninu eyiti ti àwọn ọyàn, tí àgọ́-ara ẹyin ìbímọ, fùùkû ati tí ìfun ìsàlẹ̀ wà, ni Ọ̀jọ̀gbọ́n Berzofsky ṣe àlàyé rẹ̀.
rows.output: HER2 is a protein that is overexpressed in certain types of breast cancer, including inflammatory breast cancer, in which the cancer cells invade the skin and other tissues. This overexpression is associated with a poor prognosis, as it makes the cancer more aggressive and difficult to treat.
rows.reference: HER2 "drives the growth of several types of cancer," including breast, ovarian, lung and colorectal cancers, Prof Berzofsky explained.

rows.source: O tí di àṣà báyìí láti máa fojú wa àwọn ìṣepàtàki Brexit ninu èyíkéyìí sinnima tuntun tí ó ní ọ̀rọ̀ èébú ti èdè Gẹ̀ẹ́sìti ìyẹn sì dàbí pé ó ṣ̵̵eé múlò fún ìsọjí ti àṣẹ-ìtaja ẹ̀gàn fún eré  aláwàdà-oníṣegírí ti Johnny English - eyiti o bẹ̀rẹ̀ lọ́dún 2003 ţí ó sì tún padà s'áyé lọ́dún 2011 pẹ̀lú Àtúnbi Johnny English.
rows.output: It has become a cliché to dismiss the complexities of Brexit in the new Johnny English movie, which is a parody of the James Bond series. The film, which was released in 2003, was a hit and was even revived in 2011 with the sequel Johnny English Reborn.

rows.output: In every way, the talented Johnny English has tuned his writing style to be more accessible for a second time - the title is more fun than anything else, because it is a work of art created for those who are familiar with the cinema, in the homes of those who speak English.

rows.output: I was Johnny English, a spy who was assigned to investigate the mysterious disappearance of a group of scientists who were working on a top-secret project.

rows.output: The Atkinson Award is a recognition of our work in the field of cinema, which is not only a reflection of our technical skills but also of our ability to create a story that is both entertaining and thought-provoking, similar to the work of the great filmmakers such as 007 and Mission Impossible.
rows.reference: Atkinson's gift for physical comedy is on display, but the humour feels pretty underpowered and weirdly superfluous, especially as the "serious" film brands like 007 and Mission Impossible themselves now confidently offer comedy as an ingredient.

rows.source: Ẹ̀fẹ náà dàbí pé wọ́n jú u sọ́dọ̀ àwọn ọmọdé jú ọ̀dọ̀ àwọn àgbàlagbà, àtipé fún èmi ìrìnkerindò àìtọ́ tí òmùgọ̀ Johnny English kòní àgbéjáde àti àfojúsùn bíi tí àwọn aláwàdà oníìdákẹ́jẹ́ sinnimá ninu àwọ̀n òṣère ti Bean.
rows.output: The film is a comedy that is more suitable for children than for adults, and it is a parody of the Johnny English spy series, with a lot of slapstick humor and silly antics, similar to the slapstick comedies of the 1970s.
rows.reference: The humour feels as if it is pitched at kids rather than adults, and for me Johnny English's wacky misadventures aren't as inventive and focused as Atkinson's silent-movie gags in the persona of Bean.

rows.output: And so the story goes that Johnny English, who was a lowly spy, was given the job of a high school principal, and he was not very good at it. He was more used to the rough and tumble world of espionage, where he would go undercover and get the job done. rows.source: Ninu ọdún ìkeje rẹ̀, Àjọ̀dun Ọmọ Ìlú Àgbáyé yóò rí ẹgbẹ-ẹgbẹ̀rún àwọn eniyan tó ńrọ́ lọsí Pápá Ńlá ti Central Park láti máṣe lọ gbádùn àwọn eléré bíi Janet Jackson, Cardi B àti Shawn Mendes, ṣùgbọ́n láti tún jẹ́kí àwọn eniyan mọ ìlépa tòótọ́ fún ayẹyẹ naa tííṣe fifi òpin sí ìṣẹ́ tóti bọ́sódi kí ó tó di ọdún 2030.
rows.output: In its seventh year, the Global Citizen Festival will feature a diverse lineup of artists including Janet Jackson, Cardi B, and Shawn Mendes, all of whom have been recognized as global citizens. The festival will also include a special performance by the United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres.
rows.reference: Now in its seventh year, the Global Citizen Festival will see tens of thousands of people flock to Central Park's Great Lawn to not only enjoy acts such as Janet Jackson, Cardi B and Shawn Mendes, but also to raise awareness for the event's true goal of ending extreme poverty by 2030.

rows.source: Àjọ̀dun Ọmọ Ìlú Àgbáyé náà, eyiti wọ́n bẹ̀rẹ̀ lọ́dún 2012, jẹ́ àmúgbòòrò tí Iṣẹ́ Àkànṣe ti Ìṣẹ́ Àgbáyé, ẹgbẹ́ aláàtẹnumọ́ ti àgbáyé kan ńrétí láti fòpin sí ìṣẹ́ nípa mímú iye àwọn eniyan tó ńṣiṣẹ́ gidigidi nípa dídojú ìjà kọ ọ́ pọ̀síi.
rows.output: The International Conference on the Abolition of the Death Penalty, which took place in 2012, was a major event of the International Federation of Human Rights, a network of human rights organizations from around the world that aims to abolish the death penalty through the promotion of a moratorium on executions.
rows.reference: The Global Citizen Festival, which stated in 2012, is an extension of the Global Poverty Project, an international advocacy group hoping to end poverty by increasing the number of people actively fighting against it.

rows.source: Láti leè gba tíkẹ́ẹ̀tì ọ̀fẹ́ fún ayẹyẹ náà (àyàfi bí ó báfẹ́ sán owó fún tíkẹ́ẹ̀tì ti ẸNI PÀTÀKÌ GIDI julo), àwọn tó ńlọ sí òde-eré nilati pari àwọn iṣẹ́ ṣíṣẹ̀-n-tẹ̀lé kan, tàbí ''àwọn iṣẹ́''bíi yíyọ̀ǹda ara ẹni fún iṣẹ́, kíkọ lẹ́tà i-meèlì si olórí láàgbáyé kan, ṣíṣe èyíkèyìí ninu àwọn ọ̀nà miran tóni ìtumọ́ lati jẹ́kí ìmọ̀ ìlépa wọn láti fòpin sí ìṣẹ́ pọ̀síi.
rows.output: To truly understand the world (and to truly understand the importance of the person who is the most important), those who are engaged in the business of the world must complete a series of tasks, or "works," which, if they are not done, will lead to the end of the world.
rows.reference: In order to receive a free ticket for the event (unless you were willing to pay for a VIP ticket), concertgoers had to complete a series of tasks, or "actions" such volunteering, emailing a world leader, making a phone call or any other meaningful ways to help raise awareness of their goal of ending poverty.

rows.source: Ṣùgbọn báwo ni Ọmọ Ìlú Àgbáyé ti ṣàṣeyọrí tó pẹ̀lú ọdún méjìlá tóṣẹ́kù láti mú ìlépa rẹ̀ ṣẹ?
rows.output: What is the name of the Son of the World who has been victorious with two horns to lead his people?
rows.reference: But just how successful has Global Citizen been with 12 years left to achieve its goal?

rows.source: Sé èròǹgbà fífún àwọn eniyan lérè pẹ̀lú ìpéjọpè àwọn eléré jẹ ojúlówó ọ̀nà kan rọ àwọn eniyan láti bèèrè fún ìpè kan fún iṣẹ́ ṣíṣe, tàbí i̇̀ṣẹ̀lẹ miran ti ohun tíwọ́n pè ní ''iṣẹ́ ṣíṣe bọ́tìnnì títẹ̀'' lásán - àwọn eniyan ńlérò wipr àwọn ńmú ìyàtọ̀ tóótọ̀ wá nípa bíbuwọ́lu ìbéèrè ojú-ópó ayelujara kan tàbí fífi àtẹ̀ránṣẹ́ tuwiti kan ránṣé?
rows.output: The question is, what is the true meaning of "free speech" in a world where people are constantly bombarded with information on social media, or where they are given a platform to speak but are not allowed to say anything controversial?
rows.reference: Is the idea of rewarding people with a free concert a genuine way to persuade people to demand a call for action, or just another case of so-called "clicktivism" - people feeling like they are making a true difference by signing an online petition or sending a tweet?

rows.source: Láti ọdún 2011, Ọmọ Ìlú Àgbáyé ńsọpé òun to ṣàkọsílẹ̀ ''àwọn iṣẹ́ ṣíṣe'' tó ju mílíọ̀nù mọ́kàndínlógún lọ láti ọwọ́ àwọn alàtìlẹ́yìn rẹ̀, tíwọn ńtaari àpapọ̀ àwọn ìlépa tóyàtọ̀.
rows.output: Since 2011, the World Bank has been working on a new approach to development, which is based on the idea that the best way to help people in poverty is to give them the skills and resources they need to improve their own lives.
rows.reference: Since 2011, Global Citizen says it has recorded more than 19 million "actions" from its supporters, pushing for a host of different goals.

rows.source: Ó ńsọpé àwọn iṣẹ́ ṣíṣe wọ̀nyí ti ṣe ìrànwọ́ láti ṣọ àwọn olóri àgbáyé ji láti kéde àwọn ìfiraẹnijìn àti àwọn ìlàna ètò tí ó ju bílíọ̀nù mẹ́tàdínlógójì dọ́là lọ eyiti wọ́n ti ṣètò rẹ̀ láti la ipa lórí ayé àwọn eniyan tóju bílíọ̀nù 2.25 lọ kí ó tó di ọdún 2030.
rows.output: The current rate of consumption of fossil fuels, which is projected to increase by 2.25 billion tonnes by 2030, is already having a devastating impact on the planet.
rows.reference: It says that these actions have helped spur world leaders to announce commitments and policies equating to more than $37 billion that is set to affect the lives of more than 2.25 billion people by 2030.

rows.source: Ní ìbẹ̀rẹ̀ ọdún 2018, ẹgbẹ́ náà tọ́kasí àwọn ìfarajin àti àwọn ìkéde tí ó jáde láti inu àwọn iṣẹ́ ṣíṣe rẹ̀, ó kéré tán bílíọ̀nù mẹ́wàá dọ́là ninu eyiti wọ́n ti pín tàbí tíwọn ti kójọ.
rows.output: In 2018, the group's revenue from sales and royalties was $20 billion, of which $1 billion was from streaming.
rows.reference: In early 2018, the group cited 390 commitments and announcements stemming from its actions, at least $10 billion of which have already been disbursed or fundraised.

rows.source: Ẹgbẹ́ náà ṣe àfojúdá àwọn owó tówà lábẹ́ ààbò eyiti ó ti la ipa tààrà lórí àwọn eniyan tó súnmọ́ mílíọ̀nù ẹgbẹ̀ta-léní-mọ́kàndínláàádọ́ta káàkiri àgbáyé.
rows.output: The group has been accused of laundering billions of dollars in proceeds from corruption that has affected millions of people across the world.
rows.reference: The group estimates the secured funds have so far made a direct impact on nearly 649 million people across the world.

rows.source: Àwọn kan lára àwọn ìfaraẹnijìn pàtàkì ni Agbára Oúnjẹ Jíjẹ̀, aláàjọṣiṣẹ́pọ àwọn olùdóokoòwò àti àwọn amúṣẹ́ṣe ní orilẹ-ede UK tíwọ́n farajìn fún ''ṣiṣe ìrànwọ́ fún àwọn ọmọdé láti de ibi ipá wọn lẹ́ẹ̀kúnrẹ́rẹ́,'' tó ńṣe ìlérí láti pèsè mílíọnù márùndínlógójì dọ́là gún orilẹ-ede Rwanda latí fòpin sí àìtó oúnjẹ aṣaralóore ní orilẹ-ede náà lẹ́yìn tógba àwọn àtẹ̀ránṣẹ́ tuwiti tólé ní ẹgbẹ́rùn lọ́ná máàrún dín ní ọ̀ọ́dún lọ́wọ́ Àwọn Ọmọ Ìlú Àgbáyé.
rows.output: Some of the most important humanitarian issues include the Global Hunger Index, which measures the prevalence of undernourishment, the proportion of children under five who are underweight, the proportion of children under five who are overweight, and the proportion of adults who are obese. The UK has pledged £15 million to help address these issues in Rwanda, which has one of the highest rates of malnutrition in the world. The funding will support the work of the World Food Programme, which has warned that 20 million people in the Horn of Africa are at risk of famine.
rows.reference: Some of the key commitments include The Power of Nutrition, a U.K. based partnership of investors and implementers committed to "helping children grow to their full potential," promising to provide Rwanda with $35 million to help end malnutrition in the county after receiving more than 4,700 tweets from Global Citizens.

rows.source: ''Pẹ̀lú àtìlẹ́yìn láti ọ̀dọ̀ ìjọba orilẹ-ede UK, àwọn afúnnilówó. àwọn ìjọba orilẹ-ede, àti Àwọn Ọmọ Ìlú Àgbáyé bíi ìwọ, a leè sọ àìsí ìdájọ́ òdodo ìbaṣepọ̀ ti àìtó oúnjẹ aṣaralóore dí àkọsílẹ abẹ́-ẹṣé kan ninu ìtàn,'' àṣojú Agbára ti Oúnjẹ Jíjẹ Náà Tracey Ullman sọ fún àwọm èrò nigba ìpéjọpọ̀ àwọn eléré bóti ńwáyé ní ìlú Lọndọnu ní oṣu Igbe lọ́dún 2018.
rows.output: "With the support of the UK government, the charity, the government, and the United Nations, we are able to provide a fair and transparent process for the distribution of aid," said Tracey Ullman, a representative of the charity, during a press conference in London in July 2018.
rows.reference: "With support from the UK government, donors, national governments, and Global Citizens just like you, we can make the social injustice of undernutrition a footnote in history," The Power of Nutrition ambassador Tracey Ullman told the crowd during a live concert in London in April 2018.

rows.source: Ẹgbẹ́ náà tún sọpé lẹ́yìn tí wọn ṣe àwọn iṣẹ́ ṣíṣe to ju ẹgbẹ̀rúnn máàrún lọ eyiti ó ńpè orilẹ-ede U.K. láti jẹ́kí ìmúdárasíi bá oúnjẹ jíjẹ fún àwọn ìyá àti àwọn ọmọdé, ìjọba náà kédé owó ìfifúnni fún iṣẹ́ àkànṣe kan, Agbára ti Oúnjẹ Jíjẹ, eyiti yóò leè fọwọ́kan àwọn ìyá àti àwọn ọmọdé mílíọ̀nù máàrún pẹ̀lú àwọn ìdásí oúnjẹ jíjẹ.
rows.output: The group also called for the abolition of the 10p coin, which is used in the UK to help the poor, particularly children and the elderly, who are struggling to afford food. The government has announced a new coin, the 12-sided pound coin, which will replace the 10p and 20p coins.
rows.reference: The group also said that after more than 5,000 actions were taken calling on the U.K. improve nutrition for mothers and children, the government announced funding for a project, the Power of Nutrition, that will reach 5 million women and children with nutrition interventions.

rows.source: Ní ìdáhùn sí òkan ninu àwọn ìbéèrè àwọn eniyan tówọ́pọ̀ jùlọ lori ojú-òpó rẹ̀ tó ńbéèrè ''kínni ó mú ọ ropé a leè fòpin sí ìṣẹ́ tó kọjá àlà?''
rows.output: In response to one of the most frequently asked questions by the public, which is, "What is the rope that is used to bind the universe?"
rows.reference: In response to one of the FAQs on its website asking "what makes you think we can end extreme poverty?"

rows.source: Ọmọ ìlú àgbáyé dáhùn: ''Yóò jẹ́ ọ̀nà gígùn tí ó le kan - nígbà miran a ó súbu tí a ó sì kùnà.
rows.output: The people of the world say: "You are the way, the truth, and the life.
rows.reference: Global citizen replied: "It'll be a long and hard path - sometimes we will fall and fail.

rows.source: Ṣùgbọ́n, bí àwọn ẹgbẹ́ ajàfẹ́ẹ̀tọ́-ẹni àti eyiti ó ńlódì sí ìwà ẹlẹ́yàmẹ̀yà ńlá tó saájú wa, a ó ṣàṣeyọrí, nitoripe a ni agbára púpọ̀ síi lápapọ̀.
rows.output: Ṣùgbọ́n, bí àwọ́n ẹgbẹ̀́ àjẹ̀́fọ̀tọ́-ẹni àti èyí tí ó ńlàdì sí ìwà ẹlẹ̀́yà̀mẹ̀̀yà̀ ńlá tó sàájú wa, a ó sàs̵eyọrí, nítorí pé a ní agbára púpọ̀ sí i lápapọ̀.
rows.reference: But, like the great civil rights and anti-apartheid movements before us, we will succeed, because we are more powerful together.

rows.source: Janet Jackson, àwọn The Weeknd, Shawn Mendes, Cardi B, Janelle Monáe wà lára àwọn kan ninu àwọn eléré tó ńṣeré níbi ayẹyẹ tọdún yìí ní ìlú New York, eyiti Deborah-Lee Furness àti Hugh Jackman yóò tijẹ́ àwọn olùgbàlejò.
rows.output: Janet Jackson, The Weeknd, Shawn Mendes, Cardi B, Janelle Monáe, and more will perform at the Global Citizen Festival in New York City, hosted by Deborah-Lee Furness and Hugh Jackman.
rows.reference: Janet Jackson, the Weeknd, Shawn Mendes, Cardi B, Janelle Monáe are among some of the acts performing at this year's event in New York, which will be hosted by Deborra-Lee Furness and Hugh Jackman.

rows.source: Orilẹ-ede US leè lo Àwọn Ọmọ Ogun Ojú-omi fún ''ìdèná'' lati di àwọn ìkó-ọjà agbára ti ilẹ̀ Rọ́síà jadé fún títà - Akọ̀wé Ọ̀rọ̀ Abẹ́lé
rows.output: The United States has used the Navy's "sea-based" to become a major naval force in the world - The Navy's budget is a major part of the national defense budget.
rows.reference: US could use Navy for "blockade" to hamper Russian energy exports - Interior Secretary

rows.source: Washington leè ''bí ó bá di dandan'' leè yàsí ọ̀dọ̀ Àwọn Ọmọ Ogun Ojú-omi rẹ̀ lati dènà dídé ọjà àwọn nǹkan ti ilẹ̀ Rọ́síà, àti ni Ààrin Gùngùn Ìlà-oòrun, Akọ̀wé Ọ̀rọ̀ Abẹ́lé ti orilẹ̵-ede US Ryan Zinke ti fihàn, bí Washington Examiner tí yọ ọ̀rọ̀ rẹ̀ lò.
rows.output: Washington said, "I'm willing to bet" that the Navy's 12th Fleet will be able to reach the Russian Navy's 12th Fleet, which is located in the North Pacific, according to the US Navy's official website.
rows.reference: Washington can "if necessary" resort to its Navy to prevent Russian energy hitting the markets, including in the Middle East, US Internal Secretary Ryan Zinke has revealed, as cited by Washington Examiner.

rows.source: Zinke fẹ̀sùn kàn wipe ìbáṣepọ̀ ilẹ̀ Rọ́síà pẹ̀lú ilẹ̀ Síríà - níti àkíyèsi, níbití ó ti ńṣiṣẹ́ pẹ̀lù ìfìwépe ìjọba tóbá òfin mu náà - jẹ́ ọgbọń láti ṣáwàrí àwọn ọjà fún nǹkan agbára tuntun.
rows.output: Zinke said that the Russian invasion of Syria, which has been justified by the claim that it is fighting terrorism, is actually a new attempt to secure oil resources.
rows.reference: Zinke alleged that Russia's engagement in Syria - notably, where it is operating at the invitation of the legitimate government - is a pretext to explore new energy markets.

rows.source: ''Mo gbàgbọ́ pé ìdí tíwọ́n fi wà ní Ààrin Gùngùn Ìlà-oòrun nípe wọ́n fẹ́ ṣe àdéhùn agbárs bí wọ́n tiṣe ni ìlà-oòrun Yuroopu náà, ikún gúúsù ti Yuroopu,'' ni iròyìn sọpé o sọ.
rows.output: "I agree that the idea of a Central American Confederation is a good one, just as they have done in Europe, the Southern part of Europe," he said.
rows.reference: "I believe the reason they are in the Middle East is they want to broker energy just like they do in eastern Europe, the southern belly of Europe," he has reportedly said.

rows.source: Àti pé gẹ́gẹ́ bí òṣìṣẹ́ náà ṣe sọ, ọ̀nà àbáyọ wà tí a lè fi yanjú rẹ̀.
rows.output: And as the employee said, there is a way to solve it.
rows.reference: And, according to to the official, there are ways and means to tackle it.

rows.source: “Ó sọ pé “Oriléèdè United States ní agbára nípasẹ̀ àwọn ọmọ ogun orí omi láti rí i pé àwọn ojú ọ̀nà lórí òkun wà ní ṣíṣílẹ̀,Tí ó bá sì ṣe pàtàkì, wọ́n sì lè dí i tí ó bá yẹ láti rí i dájú pé wọn kò ọ̀jà agbára wọn tà .
rows.output: He said, "The United States has the power through its naval forces to ensure that sea lanes are open, and if necessary, to block them to ensure that its vital interests are not threatened.
rows.reference: "The United States has that ability, with our Navy, to make sure the sea lanes are open, and, if necessary, to blockade, to make sure that their energy does not go to market," he said.

rows.source: Zinke ń bá àwọn ènìyàn tí ó wà níbi ìpàdé ti Ilé iṣẹ́ tí kò gbájúmọ́ eré jíjẹ Consumer Energy Alliance (Ajàfẹ́tọ̀ọ́ àwọn oníbàárà iná) ní US gbé kalẹ̀.
rows.output: Zinke is meeting with people at the Consumer Energy Alliance (Consumer Energy Alliance) meeting in the US.
rows.reference: Zinke was addressing the attendees of the event hosted by the Consumer Energy Alliance, a non-profit group which styles itself as the "voice of the energy consumer" in the US.

rows.source: Ó ṣe àfiwé ọ̀nà tí Washington ń gbà kojú orílẹ̀èdè Russia àti Iran pẹ̀lú àríwísí rẹ̀ ni pé bákan náà ni àwọn méjèèjì.
rows.output: He compared the way Washington was dealing with the country of Russia and Iran with his criticism that both were equally oppressive.
rows.reference: He went to compare Washington's approaches to dealing with Russia and Iran, noting that they are effectively the same.

rows.source: “Ó sọ pe ọ̀nà àbáyọ ni ṣíṣe àwárí irúfẹ́ epo tí orílẹ̀ èdè Russia àti Iran ní níbòmíràn. Ó tún tẹ̀síwájú pé orílẹ̀èdè Russia ò ní ohun mìíràn tí wọ́n gbójúlé fún ọrọ̀ bí kò ṣe epo.
rows.output: He said that the solution is to find a type of oil that Russia and Iran have in abundance. He also emphasized that Russia has nothing else to offer in terms of resources other than oil.
rows.reference: "The economic option on Iran and Russia is, more or less, leveraging and replacing fuels," he said, while referring to Russia as a "one trick pony" with an economy dependent on fossil fuels.

rows.source: Àwọn gbólóhùn yìí wáyé pẹ̀lú bí ìṣàkóṣo ìjọba Trump ń gbìyànjú láti fikún iye gáàsì tí ó ń tà ní Europe pẹ̀lú ìgbìyànjú láti fi ìdínwó gáàsì ti wọn lé Russia kúrò lọ́jà.
rows.output: These remarks came amid the Trump administration's efforts to increase the price of natural gas in Europe while attempting to remove Russian gas from the market.
rows.reference: The statements come as Trump administration has been on a mission to boost the export of its liquefied natural gas to Europe, replacing Russia, the far cheaper option for European consumers.

rows.source: Nítorí ìdí èyí ni àwọn òṣìṣẹ́ Ìjọba Trump àti Trump fúnra rẹ̀ ṣe ń gbìyànjú láti yí orílẹ̀èdè Germany lọ́kàn padà kí wọ́n lè jáwọ́ nínú iṣẹ́ àkànṣè Nord Stream 2 pipeline project tí Trump wòye pé òun ló mú Russia jẹ gàba lórí ìjọba Germany.
rows.output: Because of this, Trump's government and Trump himself have been trying to sway the country of Germany to get out of the Nord Stream 2 pipeline project, which Trump believes he has made Russia more powerful over the government of Germany.
rows.reference: For that effect, the Trump administration officials, including US President Donald Trump himself, try to persuade Germany to pull out of the "inappropriate" Nord Stream 2 pipeline project, which according to Trump, made Berlin Moscow's "captive."

rows.source: Moscow ti ń tẹnumọ́ pé iṣẹ́ àkànṣè Nord Stream 2 tí ó dá lórí gbígbé páìpù agbépo-rìn tí ó jẹ́ bílíọ́ọ̀nù dọ́là mọ́kànlá yóò sọ páìpù agbépo-rìn rẹ̀ di ìlọ́po méjì sí nǹkan bíi mítà kúbíìkì ọgọ́rùn-ún ó lé mẹ́wàá wáyé látàríi èròngbà wọn láti ní ìlọsíwájú nípa ètò ọrọ̀ ajé.
rows.output: Moscow has emphasized that the construction of the Nord Stream 2 pipeline, which costs around $11 billion, will double the capacity of the existing pipeline by about 10 million cubic meters per day, as they seek to advance their economic interests.
rows.reference: Moscow has repeatedly stressed that the $11 billion Nord Stream 2 pipeline, which is set to double the existing pipeline capacity to 110 billion cubic meters, is a purely economic project.

rows.source: Ìjọba Russia wòye pé ìjọba orílẹ̀èdè Amẹ́ríkà ń tako iṣẹ́ àkànṣè náà nítorí ìtara àti wọn kò fẹ́ kí Russia ní ìlọsíwájú nípa ètò ọrọ̀ ajé bíi tiwọn.
rows.output: The Russian government believes that the US government is sabotaging the project because of its popularity and does not want Russia to achieve economic success like theirs.
rows.reference: The Kremlin argues that Washington's fervent opposition to the project is simply driven by economic reasons and is an example of unfair competition.

rows.source: "Mínísítà fún ọ̀rọ̀ epo ní orílẹ̀èdè Russia Aleksandr Novak, lẹ́yìn ìpàdé rẹ̀ pẹ̀lú Sẹ́kẹ́tìrì fún ọ̀rọ̀ epo ni US tó wáyé ní oṣù kẹsàán ní Moscow sọ pé àwọn Mínísítà méjèèjì gbàgbọ́ pé epo kìí ṣe ohun tí ó tọ́ láti máa fi jẹ gàba lórí àwọn ènìyàn àti o yẹ kí àwọn oníbàárà le yan ẹnikẹ́ni tí ó bá wù wọ́n láti ra epo lọ́wọ́ rẹ̀.

rows.output: We saw the residents returning to their damaged homes to gather whatever they could find in their belongings.
rows.reference: Residents were seen returning to their destroyed homes, picking through waterlogged belongings, trying to salvage anything they could find.

rows.source: Ọ̀gọ̀ọ̀rọ̀ àwọn ènìyàn ló farapa nínú ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ ilẹ̀ mímì tí agbára rẹ̀ tó 7.5
rows.output: More than 100 people were injured in the earthquake with a magnitude of 7.5.
rows.reference: Hundreds of people were injured and hospitals, damaged by the magnitude 7.5 quake, were overwhelmed.

rows.source: Díẹ̀ nínú àwọn tó fara káṣá nínú ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ yìí, èyí tí Dwi Harris tí ó ṣìṣe léjìká ,tí egun ẹ̀yìn rẹ̀ sì kán sinmi ní iwájú ilé ìwòsàn Palu's Army, níbi tí àwọn aláìsàn ti ń rí ìtọ́jú gbà.
rows.output: Some of the first to arrive at the scene, this one by Dwi Harris, who was still conscious, his back against the wall of Palu's Army Hospital, where patients were receiving treatment.
rows.reference: Some of the injured, including Dwi Haris, who suffered a broken back and shoulder, rested outside Palu's Army Hospital, where patients were being treated outdoors due to continuing strong aftershocks.

rows.source: Pẹ̀lú omijé ni Dwi fi ń ròyìn ìṣẹ̀lẹ ilẹ̀ mímì tí ó ká òun, ọmọbìnrin àti iyawo re mọ́ àjà-ile karùn-ún ní hòtẹ́ẹ̀lì.
rows.output: With tears, Dwi recounted the earthquake that had struck her, her daughter, and her husband, leaving them with a five-month-old baby in a hotel.
rows.reference: Tears filled his eyes as he recounted feeling the violent earthquake shake the fifth-floor hotel room he shared with his wife and daughter.

rows.source: A ò ráyè kankan láti sá àsálà fún ẹ̀mí wa.
rows.output: We have no right to run away from our responsibilities.
rows.reference: "There was no time to save ourselves.

rows.source: “Láàrin ògiri tó ti wó ni mo rún mọ́” Harris sọ fún Associated Press, ó tún ṣàfikún pé ayẹyẹ ìgbéyàwó kan ló gbé òun àti ẹbí òun wá sí ìlú Palu.
rows.output: "Between the walls that have collapsed, I ran to him," Harris told the Associated Press, adding that a wedding ceremony brought him and his family to the city of Palu.
rows.reference: I was squeezed into the ruins of the wall, I think," Haris told Associated Press, adding that his family was in town for a wedding.

rows.source: “Mo kọ́kọ́ gbọ́ igbe ìyàwó mi nígbà tí ó ń kígbé fún ìrànlọ́wọ́, kí ó tó dákẹ́.
rows.output: I first heard my wife's screams when she was calling for help, before she was silenced.
rows.reference: "I heard my wife cry for help, but then silence.

rows.source: Mí ò mọ ohun tí ó ṣẹlẹ̀ sí ìyàwó àti ọmọ mi
rows.output: I don't know what happened to my wife and child.
rows.reference: I don't know what happened to her and my child.

rows.source: Mo ní ìrètí pé kò sí ohunkóhun tó ṣe wọ́n”
rows.output: I hope that nothing bad has happened to them.
rows.reference: I hope they are safe."

rows.source: Aṣojú ìjọba US ní orílẹ̀èdè China fẹ̀sùn kan orílẹ̀èdè náà pé ó ń ṣe ìpalára fún àwọn orílẹ̀èdè mìíràn pẹ̀lú pípolówó ẹ̀tàn.
rows.output: The US ambassador to China accused the country of harming other countries with its fake news.
rows.reference: U.S. ambassador accuses China of 'bullying' with 'propaganda ads'

rows.source: Lẹ́yìn ọ̀sẹ̀ kan tí ìwé ìròyìn fún ìjọba China gbé ìròyìn olójúùwé mẹ́rin kan jáde nínú ìwé ìròyìn kan ní US. Ìròyìn náà ṣe àtòólẹ̀ àǹfààní tó wà láàrin òwò láàrin China àti US, èyí tí aṣojú ìjọba náà na ìka àbùkù kan China pé ó ń fi àwọn ìwé ìròyìn orílẹ̀èdè Amẹ́ríkà tan àwọn ènìyàn.
rows.output: After a week of newspaper reports, the Chinese government released four reports in a newspaper in the US. The reports highlighted the benefits of trade between China and the US, which the Chinese government's representative criticized by calling it a "propaganda campaign" by the American media to influence public opinion.
rows.reference: A week after an official Chinese newspaper ran a four-page ad in a U.S. daily touting the mutual benefits of U.S.-China trade, the U.S. ambassador to China accused Beijing of using the American press to spread propaganda.

rows.source: U.S. Ààrẹ orílẹ̀èdè U.S. Donald Trump ní Ọjọ́rú tó kọjá tọ́ka sí ìròyìn tí China gbé jáde nínú ìwé ìròyìn Des Moines Register- ilé-iṣẹ́ ìwé ìròyìn tí ń tà jùlọ ní ìpínlẹ̀ Iowa fẹ̀sùn kan China pé ó ń gbìyànjú láti dásí ètò ìdìbò ilé fún ilé amòfin tí yóò wáyé ní ọjọ́ kẹfà oṣù kọọkànlá. Orílẹ̀èdè China kọ̀ jálẹ̀ pé àwọn kò mọwọ́-mẹsẹ̀ nípa ẹ̀sùn náà.
rows.output: U.S. President Donald Trump on Sunday accused China of trying to influence the upcoming Iowa caucuses, a key early voting event in the U.S. presidential race. The Chinese government has denied the allegations.
rows.reference: U.S. President Donald Trump last Wednesday referred to the China Daily's paid supplement in the Des Moines Register - the state of Iowa's biggest selling newspaper - after accusing China of seeking to meddle in the Nov. 6 U.S. congressional elections, a charge China denies.

rows.source: Ibu ẹnu atẹlu Trump ti Beijing n gbiyanju lati dasi ninu idibo U.S saami si ohun ti awọn osisẹ U.S sọ fun Reuters jẹ ipele tuntun ninu irusoke ipolongo ibo lọdọ Washington lati funmọ China.
rows.output: Trump's trade war with Beijing is trying to intervene in the U.S. election, according to what U.S. officials told Reuters, is a new level of escalation in the diplomatic confrontation between Washington and Beijing.
rows.reference: Trump's accusation that Beijing was trying to meddle in U.S. elections marked what U.S. officials told Reuters was a new phase in an escalating campaign by Washington to put pressure on China.

rows.source: Bí ó tilẹ̀ jẹ́ kìí ṣe ohun àràmọ̀ndà kí àwọn ìjọba òkèèrè ṣe ìpolówó fún ìlọsíwájú ọrọ̀ ajé, rògbòdìyàn nípa ọrọ̀ ajé wà láàrin Beijing ati Washington, èyí tí ó sì fà á kí àwọn méjèèjì gbé owó lórí àwọn ọjà tí ó ń wọlé láti orílẹ̀èdè kejì.
rows.output: While it is not a trade war, the economic tensions between Beijing and Washington have led both sides to impose tariffs on imports from the other country.
rows.reference: While it is normal for foreign governments to place advertisements to promote trade, Beijing and Washington are currently locked in an escalating trade war that has seen them level rounds of tariffs on each other's imports.

rows.source: Àwọn onímọ̀ lórílèedè U.S. wòye pé China ṣe àfikún owó lè ọjà tó ń wọlé sí U.S. láti orílẹ̀èdè China pàápàá jùlọ ní àwọn ìpínlẹ̀ bíi Iowa tí ó gbárùkù Trump àti ẹgbẹ́ ìṣèlú rẹ̀.
rows.output: U.S. officials believe that China is adding to its trade surplus with the U.S. by dumping goods, particularly in states like Iowa that are crucial to Trump and his political base.
rows.reference: China's retaliatory tariffs early in the trade war were designed to hit exporters in states such as Iowa that supported Trump's Republican Party, Chinese and U.S. experts have said.

rows.source: Aṣojú ìjọba U.S. ni China àti Gómìnà tẹ́lẹ̀ rí fún ìpínlẹ̀ Iowa, ẹni tí ó ń ta ohun ògbìn sí China jù, Terry Branstad sọ pé China ṣe ìpalára fún àwọn òṣìṣẹ́, okoòwò àti àgbẹ̀ nílẹ̀ Amẹ́ríkà.
rows.output: The U.S. Ambassador to China and former Governor of Iowa, Terry Branstad, said that China has harmed American workers, businesses, and farmers.
rows.reference: Terry Branstad, the U.S. ambassador to China and the former longtime governor of Iowa, a major exporter of agricultural goods to China, said Beijing had hurt American workers, farmers and businesses.

rows.source: Branstad wòye nínú ìwé tí ó kọ sínú ìwé ìròyìn Des Moines Register ní ọjọ́ Àìkú pé China ti sa gbogbo ipa wọn láti ṣe ìpolongo ẹ̀tàn nínú àwọn ilé iṣẹ́ ìròyìn ní Amẹ́ríkà.
rows.output: Branstad wrote in an op-ed column in the Des Moines Register on Sunday that China has used its influence to promote propaganda in American media.
rows.reference: China, Branstad wrote in an opinion piece in Sunday's Des Moines Register, "is now doubling down on that bullying by running propaganda ads in our own free press."

rows.source: "Ìjọba China ń ṣe àmúlò ètò ìròyìn tí kò ní ìpalára láti ọ̀dọ̀ ìjọba tí ó wà ní Amẹ́ríkà láti sanwó ṣe ìpolongo ẹ̀tàn àti irọ́ nínú ìwé ìròyìn Des Moines Register,” ni ohun tí Branstad kọ.
rows.output: "The Chinese government is using a propaganda program funded by the American government to pay for ads and editorials in the Des Moines Register," wrote Branstad.
rows.reference: "In disseminating its propaganda, China's government is availing itself of America's cherished tradition of free speech and a free press by placing a paid advertisement in the Des Moines Register," Branstad wrote.

rows.source: "Ó tún tẹ̀síwájú pé “Lódì kejì ẹ̀wẹ̀, kò fi bẹ́ẹ̀ sí àwọn alátakò tàbí ààfihàn èrò àwọn ará China lórí irúfẹ́ ọwọ́ ti ìjọba fi mú ètò ọrọ̀ ajé. Èyí rí bẹ́ẹ̀ nítorí abẹ́ ìṣàkóso ẹgbẹ́ ìṣèlú Chinese Communist Party ni àwọn ilé iṣẹ́ ìròyìn wà.
rows.output: "It also continued that "The second wave of the virus, however, did not have any impact on the Chinese Communist Party or the Chinese government's policies on the type of economic system. This is because the Chinese Communist Party's control over the media outlets was maintained.
rows.reference: "In contrast, at the newsstand down the street here in Beijing, you will find limited dissenting voices and will not see any true reflection of the disparate opinions that the Chinese people may have on China's troubling economic trajectory, given that media is under the firm thumb of the Chinese Communist Party," he wrote.

rows.source: Ó tún fikún un pé ọ̀kan nínú àwọn ògbóntarìgì ilé ìwé ìròyìn ní orílẹ̀èdè China kọ̀ jálẹ̀ láti tẹ iṣẹ́ òun sínú ìwé ìròyìn wọn bí ó tilẹ̀ jẹ́ pé Branstad kò dárúkọ ìwé ìròyìn náà ní pàtó.
rows.output: He also added that one of the state-run news agencies in China refused to publish his work even though Branstad did not mention the news agency specifically.
rows.reference: He added that "one of China's most prominent newspapers dodged the offer to publish" his article, although he did not say which newspaper.

rows.source: Ẹgbẹ́ Ìṣèlú Rìpúbílíkáànì ń ya àwọn obìnrin kúrò pẹ̀lú ọ̀rọ̀ Kavanaugh, Àwọn Onímọ̀ kìlọ̀
rows.output: The Republican Party is splitting women from the issue of Kavanaugh, Scientists warn
rows.reference: Republicans Alienating Women Voters Ahead of Midterms With Kavanaugh Debacle, Analysts Warn

rows.source: Pẹ̀lú bí ọ̀pọ̀ nínú àwọn àgbà ọ̀jẹ̀ olóṣèlú ẹgbẹ́ republican ṣe ń gbárùkù ẹni tí wọ́n yàn ní ilé ẹjọ́ tí ó ga jù lọ pẹ̀lú gbogbo àwọn ẹ̀sùn ìfipábóbìnrin lòpọ̀, àwọn onímọ̀ tí ń kìlọ̀ pé ọ̀rọ̀ yìí yóò lẹ́yìn pàápàá jùlọ láti ọwọ́ àwọn obìnrin nínú ètò ìdìbò áàrin táàmù.
rows.output: With many of the old guard Republicans now endorsing the Supreme Court nominee with all sorts of allegations of sexual misconduct, experts are warning that this issue will particularly affect women in the midterms.
rows.reference: As many top Republicans stand-by and defend Supreme Court nominee Brett Kavanaugh in the face of several allegations of sexual assault, analyst have warned they will see a backlash, particularly from women, during the upcoming midterm elections.

rows.source: Ọ̀rọ̀ náà ti fa ọ̀pọ̀lọ̀pọ̀ rúkèrúdò, àwọn ọmọ ẹgbẹ́ ìṣèlú Rìpúbílíkáànì sì ń takú àwọn yóò tún dìbò fún àwọn ọmọ ẹgbẹ́ wọn.
rows.output: The statement has caused a lot of controversy, and Republican lawmakers are threatening to vote against their own party members.
rows.reference: The emotions surrounding this have been extremely high, and most Republicans are on record already showing they wanted to go forward with a vote.

rows.source: Ọ̀jọ̀gbọ́n nínú ẹ̀kọ́ ìṣèlú ní Maxwell School tí ó wà ní Yunifásítì Syracuse Grant Reheer ṣọ fún àwọn ìwé ìròyìn The Hill lọ́jọ́ Àbámẹ́ta pé ọ̀rọ̀ náà yóò lẹ́yìn.
rows.output: Professor of political science at the Maxwell School at Syracuse University Grant Reeher defended the media outlets The Hill on Monday that the term would be used.
rows.reference: Those things can't be walked back," Grant Reeher, a professor of political science at Syracuse University's Maxwell School told The Hill for an article published Saturday.

rows.source: Reheer sọ pé òun kò rò bóyá ìgbésẹ̀ tí Amòfin Jeff Flake (R-Arizona) nípa pípè àjọ FBI láti wá ṣe ìwádìí àwọn ẹ̀sùn tí wọ́n fi kan Kavanaugh yóò tó láti pẹ̀tù sọ́kàn àwọn olùdìbò tí inú ń bí lọ́wọ́ lórí ọ̀rọ̀ náà.
rows.output: Reheer said he didn't think the action by Attorney Jeff Flake (R-Arizona) of calling the FBI to investigate the allegations against Kavanaugh would be enough to sway the voters who are already decided on the issue.
rows.reference: Reeher said he doubts Senator Jeff Flake's (R-Arizona) last-minute push for an FBI investigation will be enough to placate angry voters.

rows.source: "“Àwọn obìnrin ò ní gbàgbé ohun tí ó ṣẹlẹ̀ ní àná, wọn kò ní gbàgbé rẹ̀ lónìí, wọn kò sì ní gbàgbé rẹ̀ nínú ètò ìdìbò tí yóò wáyé ní oṣù kọọkànlá” ni ohun tí Karine Jean-Pierre, olùbádámọ̀ràn àgbà àti agbẹnusọ gbogbo fún ẹgbẹ́ MoveOn sọ lọ́jọ Ẹtì, èyí tí ó sì jẹyọ nínú ìwé ìròyìn Washington, D.C.
rows.output: "“Women will not forget what happened yesterday, they will not forget it today, and they will not forget it in the electoral process that will take place in November” said Karine Jean-Pierre, a senior adviser and spokesperson for the progressive group MoveOn, on Sunday, which was reported in the Washington, D.C.
rows.reference: "Women are not going to forget what happened yesterday - they are not going to forget it tomorrow and not in November," Karine Jean-Pierre, a senior adviser and national spokeswoman for the progressive group MoveOn said on Friday, according to the Washington, D.C. newspaper.

rows.source: Oṣù kọọkànlá ń bọ̀! Ní ohun tí àwọn afẹ̀hónúhàn ń ké bí wọ́n ṣe fi ìtaara wọn hàn ní ilé Aṣòfin pẹ̀lú bí àwọn ọmọ ẹgbẹ́ ìṣèlú Rìpúbílíkáànì tí ó wà ní ìgbìmọ̀ tó ń ṣàkóso ọ̀rọ̀ ilé ẹjọ́ ṣe ń tẹ̀síwájú láti yan Kavanaugh sípò. The Mic jẹ́ kí ó yé wa pé èyí wáyé lẹ́yìn ẹ̀rí dọ́kítà Christine Blasey Ford. Christine Blasey Ford, Mic ní ó ń jọ́bọ̀ ìròyìn.
rows.output: November is coming! The Mic is here to tell you that this is happening after the testimony of Dr. Christine Blasey Ford. Christine Blasey Ford, the Mic is here to tell you, is a credible witness.
rows.reference: On Friday morning, protestors chanted "November is coming!" as they demonstrated in the hallway of the Senate as the Republicans controlling the Judiciary Committee chose to move forward with Kavanaugh's nomination despite the testimony of Dr. Christine Blasey Ford, Mic reported.

rows.source: Onímọ̀ ìṣèlú Stu Rothenberg sọ “Ìmọ̀sílára kò ní í sí lára àwọn ènìyàn, èyí yóò sì mú wọn dìbò”
rows.output: Political analyst Stu Rothenberg said "The public is not paying attention, and that will cost them."
rows.reference: "Democratic enthusiasm and motivation is going to be off the chart," Stu Rothenberg, a nonpartisan political analyst, told the news site.

rows.source: Àwọn ènìyàn tilẹ̀ ti ń sọ pé àwọn kò lè dúró kí ọjọ́ ìdìbò dé.
rows.output: People are already saying that they can't wait for the election day.
rows.reference: "People are saying it's already been high; that's true.

rows.source: Ó ṣeéṣe kí ìmọ̀sílára pọ̀ sí pàápàá jùlọ láàrin àwọn obìnrin tí ó wà ní ìgbèríko àti àwọn ọmọbìnrin láàrin ọmọ ọdún méjìdínlógún sí óòkandínlọ́gbọ̀n tí wọ́n ò nífẹ̀ẹ́ ààrẹ, síbẹ̀ tí wọ́n kìí dìbò.”
rows.output: It is possible that the sense of entitlement is particularly strong among women in the region and among girls between the ages of 18 and 29 who do not like the president, but do not vote.
rows.reference: But it could be higher, particularly among swing women voters in the suburbs and younger voters, 18- to 29-year-olds, who while they don't like the president, often don't vote."

rows.source: Kí Ford tó jẹ́rìí ní gbangba nípa ẹ̀sùn ìfipábóbìnrin lòpọ̀ tí ó fi kan Kavanaugh ni àwọn onímọ̀ ti ń kìlọ̀ pé ó ṣeéṣe kí yíyan Kavanaugh sípò bu ẹgbẹ́ ìṣèlú Rìpúbílíkáànì lọ́wọ́.
rows.output: Before Ford's public testimony about the alleged sexual assault by Kavanaugh, some experts warned that confirming Kavanaugh to the Supreme Court could be a major setback for the Republican Party.
rows.reference: Even before Ford's public testimony detailing her allegations of sexual assault against the Supreme Court nominee, analysts suggested a backlash could follow if Republicans pushed forward with the confirmation.

rows.source: “Ọ̀rọ̀ yìí ti dá yánpọyánrin kalẹ̀ fún ẹgbẹ́ wa” ni ohun tí Michael Steele tí ó fìgbà kan jẹ́ alága fún ìgbìmọ̀ gbogbogbò ní ẹgbẹ́ ìṣèlú Rìpúbílíkáànì sọ ní ọ̀sẹ̀ tó kọjá gẹ́gẹ́ bí NBC News ṣe sọ.
rows.output: "This phrase has been used to galvanize our base" is what Michael Steele, former chairman of the Republican National Committee, said last week as NBC News reported.
rows.reference: "This has become a muddled mess for the GOP," said Michael Steele, former chairman of the Republican National Committee, early last week, according to NBC News.

rows.source: “Ọ̀rọ̀ yìí kìí ṣe nípa bóyá àwọn ẹgbẹ́ ìṣèlú Rìpúbílíkáànì yan Kavanaugh sípò nìkan, ó tún nííṣe pẹ̀lú ọwọ́ tí ẹgbẹ́ ìṣèlú Rìpúbílíkáànì fi mú ọ̀rọ̀ náà àti ọwọ́ tí wọ́n fi mú Ford” Olùdarí ẹgbẹ́ tó ń ṣe ìrànlọ́wọ́ fún ẹgbẹ́ ìṣèlú Dẹ́mókírààtì Priorities USA, Guy Cecil ló sọ èyí fún ilé iṣẹ́ ìròyìn náà.
rows.output: "This statement is not just about whether the Republican Party nominated Kavanaugh, but also about the role of the Republican Party in pushing the narrative and the role they played in pushing Ford."
rows.reference: "It's just not about the committee vote or the final vote or whether Kavanaugh is put on the bench, it's also about the way Republicans have handled this and how they have treated her," Guy Cecil, director of Priorities USA, a group that helps to elect Democrats, pointed out to the news channel.

rows.source: Síbẹ̀, èrò àwọn ọmọ Amẹ́ríkà pín sí méjì lórí ọ̀rọ̀ náà pẹ̀lú bí wọn kò mọ ẹni tí ó yẹ kí wọ́n gbàgbọ́ nínú Kavanaugh àti Ford.
rows.output: However, American public opinion is divided on the issue with many people unsure of who to believe in Kavanaugh and Ford.
rows.reference: However, Americans appear to be somewhat split over who to believe in the wake of Ford's and Kavanaugh's testimonies, with slightly more siding with the latter.

rows.source: Ìdìbò afèròhàn tí YouGov gbé kalẹ̀ fi hàn pé ìdá mọ́kànlelógoji nínú àwọn tó kópa nínú ètò ìdìbò náà sọ pé àwọn gba Ford gbọ́ nígbà tí ìdá márùndínlógójì ló sọ pé àwọn gba Kavanaugh gbọ́.
rows.output: The YouGov poll found that 46% of respondents said they trust Ford, while 54% said they trust Kavanaugh.
rows.reference: A new poll from YouGov shows that 41 percent of respondents definitely or probably believed Ford's testimony, while 35 percent said they definitely or probably believed Kavanaugh.

rows.source: Ìdá méjìdínlógójì ló sọ pé àwọn ní ìgbàgbọ́ pé ó ṣeéṣe kí Kavanaugh ti parọ́ nínú ẹ̀rí rẹ̀ nígbà tí ìdá ọgbọ̀n ló gbàgbọ́ pé ó ṣeéṣe kí Ford ti parọ́ nínú ẹ̀rí tirẹ̀ bákan náà.
rows.output: 48% believe it is likely that Kavanaugh lied under oath, while 30% believe it is likely that Ford lied under oath.
rows.reference: Additionally, 38 percent said they thought Kavanaugh has probably or definitely lied during his testimony, while just 30 percent said the same about Ford.

rows.source: The Guardian ròyìn pé lẹ́yìn tí amòfin Flake ké sí àjọ FBI, ìwádìí ti ń lọ lọ́wọ́ lórí ẹ̀sùn tí Ford and afẹ̀sùkan mìíràn Deborah Ramírez fi kan Kavanaugh.
rows.output: The Guardian reported that after Senator Flake called the FBI, the investigation was continuing on the allegations against Ford and another accuser, Deborah Ramirez, against Kavanaugh.
rows.reference: After the push from Flake, the FBI is currently investigating the allegations brought forward by Ford as well as at least one other accuser, Deborah Ramirez, The Guardian reported.

rows.source: Ford jẹ́rìí níwájú ìgbìmọ̀ tó ń rí sí ilé ẹjọ́ nílé Aṣòfin pé Kavanaugh mú ọtí yó, ó sì fipá bá òun lòpọ̀ nígbà tí òun pé ọmọ ọdún mẹ́tàdínlógún.
rows.output: Ford testified before the Senate Judiciary Committee that Kavanaugh had sexually assaulted her when she was 15 years old.
rows.reference: Ford testified before the Senate Judiciary Committee under oath last week that Kavanaugh drunkenly assaulted her at the age of 17.

rows.source: Ramirez ṣàlàyé pé Kavanaugh ṣí nǹkan ọmọkùnrin rẹ̀ fún òun láti rí nígbà tí wọ́n ń dìjọ kẹ́kọ̀ọ́ ní Yale. Èyí ṣẹlẹ̀ ni patí kan tí wọ́n lọ láàrin ọdún 1980 síwájú sí i.
rows.output: Ramirez explained that Kavanaugh opened a door for him to see when they were studying at Yale. This happened in one of the years between 1980 and 1982.

rows.source: Olùdásílẹ Ìtàkùǹ Àyélujára ń gbèrò láti Bẹ̀rẹ̀ Íntánẹ̀ẹ̀tì Tuntun kan láti lé Mú Google àti Facebook
rows.output: The Internet Archive's founder is considering starting a new Internet to replace Google and Facebook.
rows.reference: The Inventor of the World Wide Web Plans to Start a New Internet to Take on Google and Facebook

rows.source: Tim Berners-Lee, olùdásílẹ̀ Ìtàkùn ayélujára, ń ṣe ifilọ́lẹ̀ ìbẹ̀rẹ̀ kan tí ó máa jẹ́ orogún pẹ̀lú Facebook, Amazon àti Google.
rows.output: Tim Berners-Lee, the creator of the World Wide Web, is launching a new project that will be funded by Facebook, Amazon, and Google.
rows.reference: Tim Berners-Lee, the inventor of the World Wide Web, is launching a startup that seeks to rival Facebook, Amazon and Google.

rows.source: Iṣẹ́ àkànṣe Ògbóǹtarìgì onímọ̀ ẹ̀rọ, Inrupt, jẹ́ ilé iṣẹ́ tí ó dúró lórí i orísun ìpìlẹ̀ iṣẹ́ Berners-Lee.
rows.output: The World Wide Web project, Inrupt, is a company based on the foundation's intellectual property.
rows.reference: The technology legend's latest project, Inrupt, is a company that builds off of Berners-Lee's open source platform Solid.

rows.source: Solid fààyè gba àwọn aṣàmúlò láti yan ibi tí dátà wọn yóò di fífipamọ́ sí àti àwọn ènìyàn wo ní wọ́n le ráyè sí àti irú ìwífún tí wọ́n le ráyè sí.
rows.output: Solid fay offers users the ability to choose where their data is stored and who can access it, and what type of information they can access.
rows.reference: Solid allows users to choose where their data is stored and what people are allowed to have access to what information.

rows.source: Nínú ìfọ̀rọ̀wánilẹ́nuwò pẹ́lú ilé iṣẹ́ Fast, Berners-Lee ṣàwàdà pé èròńgbà lẹ́yìn Inrupt ni láti le “jẹ gàba lórí ayé.”
rows.output: In an interview with Fast Company, Berners-Lee joked that the idea behind Inrupt was to "be the biggest company in the world."
rows.reference: In an exclusive interview with Fast Company, Berners-Lee joked that the intent behind Inrupt is "world domination."

rows.source: “A gbọ́dọ̀ ṣe báyìí," ó sọ bẹ́ẹ̀ nípa ìbẹ̀rẹ̀ náà.
rows.output: "We have to do this now," he said, about the start.
rows.reference: "We have to do it now," he said of the startup.

rows.source: "Ó jẹ́ àkókò onítàn."
rows.output: "It's a time of great change."
rows.reference: "It's a historical moment."

rows.source: Ìṣàfilọ́̀lẹ̀ náà ń lo ìmọ̀ ẹ̀rọ Solid láti fààyègba àwọn ènìyàn láti ṣẹ̀dá “ilé ìtàjà dátà adáni lórí ayélujára” tàbí POD.
rows.output: The initiative uses Solid's technology to enable individuals to create their own "personal data stores online" or PODs.
rows.reference: The app uses Solid's technology to allow people to create their own "personal online data store" or a POD.

rows.source: Ó le ní àwọn àtòkọ olùbásọ̀rọ̀, ohun-àti-ṣe, kàlẹ́ńdà, ibi ìpamọ́ orin àti àwọn irinṣẹ́ àdáni àti àfyṣiṣẹ́ mìràn.
rows.output: It may have contact lists, to-dos, calendars, music storage, and other custom and third-party tools.
rows.reference: It can contain contact lists, to-do lists, calendar, music library and other personal and professional tools.

rows.source: Ó dábí Google Drive, Microsoft Outlook, Slack àti Spotify tí gbogbo wọ́n wà nílẹ̀ lórí aṣawákiri ní àṣìkò kannáà.
rows.output: It looks like Google Drive, Microsoft Outlook, Slack, and Spotify are all available on the browser at the same time.
rows.reference: It's like Google Drive, Microsoft Outlook, Slack and Spotify are all available on one browser and all at the same time.

rows.source: Ohun tí ó dá yàtọ̀ nípa ilé ìtàjà dátà àdáni ayelujára pé aṣàmúlò ló kù sí lọ́wọ́ láti mọ ẹni tí ó le ráyèsí àti irú ìwífún tó le ráyèsí.
rows.output: The unique thing about the global data market is that the consumer still has the power to decide what information they want to access.
rows.reference: What's unique about the personal online data store is that it is completely up to the user who can access what kind of information.

rows.source: Ilé iṣẹ́ pè ní “Ìrónilágbára àdáni nípaṣẹ̀ dátà.”
rows.output: The company is called "Data-Driven Decision-Making."
rows.reference: The company calls it "personal empowerment through data."

rows.source: Èròńgbà fún Inrupt, gẹ́gẹ́bí Olùdásílẹ̀ ilé iṣẹ́ náà John Bruce ṣe sọ, ni pé ó wá fún ilé iṣẹ̀ láti mú àwọn ohun àmúlò, ìlànà àti àwọn ọgbọ́n àtinúdá láti ṣèrànwọ́ láti mú kí Solid wà nílẹ̀ fún gbogbo ènìyàn.
rows.output: The purpose of Inrupt, as stated by the founder of the company John Bruce, is to bring tools, processes, and technologies to bear to help make Solid real for everyone.
rows.reference: The idea for Inrupt, according to the company's CEO John Bruce, is for the company to bring resources, process and appropriate skills to help make Solid available to everyone.

rows.source: Ilé iṣẹ́ náà ní Berners-Lee, Bruce, ètò ìpèsè ààbò tí IBM rà, àwọn òṣìṣẹ́ fúngbàdíẹ̀ tí wọ́n gbà láti ṣiṣẹ́ lórí iṣẹ́ àkànṣe náà, àti àwùjọ àwọn akọkóòdù tí wọ́n jẹ́ olùfarajìn.
rows.output: The project was funded by IBM, and included Berners-Lee, Bruce, a security software company, a small team of employees hired to work on the project, and a community of volunteer developers.
rows.reference: The company currently consists of Berners-Lee, Bruce, a security platform bought by IBM, some on-staff developers contracted to work on the project, and a community of volunteer coders.

rows.source: Bẹ́rẹ̀ láti ọ̀ṣẹ̀ yìí, àwọn aṣàmúàgbà ìmọ̀ ẹ̀rọ káàkiri àgbáyé le ṣldá àwọn ìṣàfilọ́lẹ̀ tiwọ́n ní àkàtà wọ́n nípa lílo àwọn irínṣẹ́ tó wà nílẹ̀ lórí wẹ́ẹ̀bù Inrupt.
rows.output: Starting this month, global tech leaders can create their own decentralized apps using Inrupt's tools available on the web.
rows.reference: Starting this week, technology developers around the world could create their own decentralized apps using the tools available on the Inrupt website.

rows.source: Berners-Lee sọ pé òun àti àwọn akẹgbẹ́ rẹ̀ kò bá “Facebook àti Google” sọ̀rọ̀ nípa bóyá tàbí ki wọ́n ṣètò ìyípadà pátápátá níbi gbogbo àwòṣe òkòwò wọn tí máa yípadà tàbí kí ó soríkodò láìròtẹ́lẹ̀.
rows.output: Berners-Lee said that he and his colleagues did not talk to "Facebook and Google" about whether or not to make a fundamental change to all their commercial models that would be irreversible.
rows.reference: Berners-Lee said that he and his team are not talking to "Facebook and Google about whether or not to introduce a complete change where all their business models are completely upended overnight.

rows.source: "Àwa kò bèèrè fún ìyànda wọn."
rows.output: "We do not need their mercy."
rows.reference: "We are not asking their permission."

rows.source: Nínú àtljíṣẹ́ lórí Medium tí wọ́n tẹ̀jáde ní sátidé, Berners-Lee kọ lórí Inrupts pé “àfojúsùn ni láti pèsè ohun àmúṣagbara olókòwò àti àyíká ilegbèè láti ṣèrànwọ́ ìdáàbòbò àti àmúyẹ wẹ́ẹ̀bù tí a fi Solid ṣe.”
rows.output: In a Medium post published on Saturday, Berners-Lee wrote on Inrupts that "the goal is to provide a free, open, and sustainable platform to help secure and enhance the web that Solid enables."
rows.reference: In a post on Medium published on Saturday, Berners-Lee wrote that Inrupt's "mission is to provide commercial energy and an ecosystem to help protect the integrity and quality of the new web built on Solid."

rows.source: Ní 1994, Berners-Lee tí Ítánẹ̀ẹ̀tì padà nígbàtí ó dá ilé iṣẹ́ wẹ́ẹ̀bù ayélujára sílẹ̀ ní ilé ẹ̀kọ́ ìmọ̀ ẹ̀rọ ní Massachusetts.
rows.output: In 1994, Berners-Lee returned to academia when he founded the World Wide Web Consortium at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.
rows.reference: In 1994, Berners-Lee transformed the Internet when he established the World Wide Web Consortium at Massachusetts Institute of Technology.

rows.source: Ní àwọn oṣù bí díẹ̀ ṣẹ́yìn, Berners-Lee ni ó ti jẹ́ ẹní àwòkọ́ṣe níbi ìjíròrò aláìṣègbè.
rows.output: In recent months, Berners-Lee has been a vocal critic in the debate over net neutrality.
rows.reference: In recent months, Berners-Lee has been an influential voice in the net neutrality debate.

rows.source: Kódà lákòókò ìṣàfilọ́lẹ̀ Inrupt, Berners-Lee sì máa jẹ́ Olùdásílẹ̀ àti Olùdarí ilé iṣẹ́ wẹ́ẹ̀bù ayélujára, ìpìlẹ̀ Wẹ́ẹ̀bù àti ilé iṣẹ́ Dátà Àjọlò.
rows.output: Even during the launch of Inrupt, Berners-Lee would remain the Founder and Director of the World Wide Web Consortium, the foundation of the Web and the Internet Data Consortium.
rows.reference: Even while launching Inrupt, Berners-Lee will remain the Founder and Director of World Wide Web Consortium, the Web Foundation and the Open Data Institute.

rows.source: "Mó ní ìrétí ayọ lórí sáà tó ń bọ̀ yìí lórí wẹ́ẹ̀bù,” Bermers-Lee ṣàfikún ọ̀rọ̀.
rows.output: "I'm also excited about the upcoming events on the web," Bermers-Lee added.
rows.reference: "I'm incredibly optimistic for this next era of the web," Berners-Lee added.

rows.source: Bernard Vann: Àlùfàá Victoria Cross ti WW1 ní wọ́n ṣayẹyẹ rẹ̀ ṣayẹyẹ rẹ̀
rows.output: Bernard Vann: The WW1 Victoria Cross recipient was honored with a statue

rows.source: Àlùfáà Sọ́ọ̀sì kannáà tí ó wà ní ilẹ̀ Gẹ́ẹ̀sí tó jẹ ẹ̀bún Victoria Cross lákòókò Ogun Àgbáyé Àkọ́kọ́ bí jagunjagun ni wọn ti ṣayẹyẹ rẹ̀ ní ilú abínibí rẹ́ lẹ́yín bí 100.
rows.output: The Bishop of Soissons, who was awarded the Victoria Cross during World War I, was honored in his home town after 100 years.
rows.reference: The only Church of England cleric to win a Victoria Cross during World War One as a combatant has been celebrated in his hometown 100 years on.

rows.source: Lt Col The Reverend Bernard Vann gba àmì ẹ̀yẹ náà ní oṣù kẹsàn án 1918 nínú ìkọlù ní Bellenglise àti Lehaucourt.

rows.reference: Lt Col The Reverend Bernard Vann won the award on 29 September 1918 in the attack at Bellenglise and Lehaucourt.

rows.source: Síbẹ̀síbẹ̀, asọnipa kán ló pa á ní bí ọjọ̀ mẹ́rin lẹ́yìn náà tí kò sí mọ̀ pé ó ti jẹ ẹ̀bùn tó ga jùlọ nínú ọ́wọ̀ tó ga jùlọ nínú ilé iṣẹ́ ológun tí ilẹ̀ Gẹ́ẹ̀sì.
rows.output: However, he was shot in the back four days later, without knowing that he had been awarded the highest honor in the British military.

rows.source: Òkúta ìṣèrántí ní àwọn ọmọ rẹ̀ méjèèjì fi lọ́lẹ̀ ní ibi ìtólẹ́ṣẹ́ ẹ̀yẹ ní Rushden, Northamptonshire, ní Sátidé.
rows.output: The memorial stone was unveiled by her two sons at the Rushden Memorial, Northamptonshire, on Saturday.

rows.source: Gẹ́gẹ́bí Gásẹ́ẹ̀tì London, ní 29 oṣù kẹsàn án 1918, Lt Col Van ló saájú ìkọ̀ àwọn ọmọ ogun ní ìkọjá Canal de Saint-Quentin “láàrin kurukuru tó nípọ̀n àti lábẹ́ ẹ iná ńlá ńla láti ara àwọn ìbọ́n ẹlẹ́rọ ńlá."

rows.reference: Lawyer Christian Schertz said the player would seek compensation for "moral damages in an amount corresponding to the gravity of the infringement, which is probably one of the most serious violations of personal rights in recent years."

rows.source: Ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ ìfẹ́sùnkanni náà ní wọ́n sọ pé ó wáyé ní ọṣù kẹfà 2009 ní Ilé ìtura Palms àt Casino ni Las Vegas.
rows.output: The incident of the kidnapping occurred in June 2009 at the Palms Hotel and Casino in Las Vegas.
rows.reference: The alleged incident is said to have taken place in June 2009 at a suite at the Palms Hotel and Casino in Las Vegas.

rows.source: Lẹ́yìn tí wọ́n ti padé ní pátí alẹ́, Ronaldao àti Mayorga ní wọ́n jábọ̀ pé wọn padà sí yàrá agbábọ̀ọ̀lù náà., níbi tí wọn ti fé ẹ̀sùn tí kò tíì lẹ́rìí k[sn pé ó fi ìpa báá a lòpọ̀ láti fùrọ̀, gẹ́gẹ́bí àkọ̀sílẹ̀ ìwé tí wọ̀n kọ ní Ilé ẹjọ Agbègbe Clark ní́ Nevada.
rows.output: After meeting in the evening, Ronaldao and Mayorga were arrested and charged with returning to the ballroom, where they were accused of having sex, as stated in the unverified written statement filed in Clark County Court in Nevada.
rows.reference: After meeting in a nightclub, Ronaldo and Mayorga reportedly went back to the player's room, where he allegedly anally raped her, according to papers filed at Clark County District Court in Nevada.

rows.source: Mayorga sọ wípé Ronaldo wólẹ̀ níwájú òhun lẹ́yìn ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ náà tí ó sì sọ fún òun pé “99 ìdá ọgọ́rùn ún” ní òun fi jẹ́ “ọkùrin rere” tí “ìdá kan l’ọ́gọ́rù ún” sì já òhun kulẹ̀.
rows.output: Mayorga said Ronaldo tripped over him after the incident and told him he was "99 percent" a "good guy" and "one percent" tripped him up.
rows.reference: Mayorga claims Ronaldo fell to his knees after the alleged incident and told her he was "99 percent" a "good guy" let down by the "one percent."

rows.source: Àwọn àkọsílẹ̀ fi yé wa pé Ronaldo fi ìdí rẹ̀ múlẹ̀ pé àwọn méjèèjì ní ìbálòpọ̀, ṣùgbọ́n àjọ̀mọ̀àwọn méjèèjì ní.
rows.output: The records show that Ronaldo admitted that both of them had sexual relations, but the couple were not married.
rows.reference: The documents claim that Ronaldo confirmed the pair had sex, but that it was consensual.

rows.source: Mayorga tún sọ bákan náà pé òun lọ sí t’ọlọ́pàá àtipé òun yà àwọn àwòrán ìpalára tí òun ní ní ìlé ìwòsàn kan, ṣùgbọ́n tí òwun gbà láti yanjú ọ̀rọ̀ náà lábẹ́lé nítorípé òwn “ẹ̀rù gbíga ẹ̀sàn bà á” àtí pé òun ní àibàlẹ̀ ọkàn nípa “ìdójútì káríáyé”
rows.output: Mayorga also said that he went to the police station and took pictures of the damage to his car, but he agreed to settle the matter quietly because he was "scared of the consequences" and had "a weak heart about the international incident."
rows.reference: Mayorga also claims she went to the police and had photographs taken of her injuries at a hospital, but later agreed to an out-of-court settlement because she felt "terrified of retaliation" and was worried about "being publicly humiliated."

rows.source: ẹni ọgbọ̀n ọdún ó lé mẹ́rin náà sọ pé òun ṣẹṣẹ̀ ń wá bíòun ṣe máa yí ìpínnu náà padà ní nítorí ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ náà ni ó ń jẹ́ ọgbẹ́ ọkàn fún òun.
rows.output: A thirty-year-old man said that he was just starting to figure out how to change his decision because the event was still hurting him in the heart.
rows.reference: The 34-year-old says she is now seeking to overturn the settlement as she continues to be traumatized by the alleged incident.

rows.source: Ronaldo ṣẹ̀ṣẹ̀ fẹ́ darapọ̀ mọ́ Real Madrid láti Manchester United ni àkókò ìkọlù náà, àtipé ní sọ́mà yìí ló lọ sí òmìràn ìtálí Juve nínú ìṣòwò €100.
rows.output: Ronaldo had just joined Real Madrid from Manchester United at the time of the transfer, and this was the first time he was facing the other great Italian team in the market €100.
rows.reference: Ronaldo was on the verge of joining Real Madrid from Manchester United at the time of the alleged assault, and this summer moved to Italian giants Juve in a €100 million deal.

rows.source: Brexit: UK ‘má kábámọ̀ títí ayé’ nípa pípàdńu àwọn àṣemọ́tò
rows.output: Brexit: UK 'will not be swayed by any means' on customs union
rows.reference: Brexit: UK 'would forever regret' losing carmakers

rows.source: Orílẹ̀ èdè UK "má kábámọ̀ títí ayé" tí ó bá sọ ipò rẹ̀ nù bíi olórí lágbàáyé nínú mọ́tò ṣiṣẹ́ lẹ́yìn Brexit, àkswé fún okòòwò Greg Clark ló sọ bẹ́ẹ.
rows.output: The UK government "will not be embarrassed" if it fails to become the world's leading motor industry power after Brexit, Trade Secretary Greg Clark said.
rows.reference: The UK "would regret it forever" if it lost its status as a world leader in car manufacturing after Brexit, Business Secretary Greg Clark has said.

rows.source: Ótún sọ síwájú pé “nípa” pé Toyota UK ti sọ fún BBC pé tí Bírítéénì bá fi EU sílẹ̀ láì ní àdéhùn ìsòwò tó só pọ̀, ó máa ṣe ìdádúró ìgbéjáde-iṣẹ̀ ní ilé iṣẹ́ rẹ̀ ní Burnaston, ní ẹ̀bá Derby.
rows.output: The company said that "in the event" of a British exit from the EU without a trade agreement, it would halt production at its Burnaston plant, near Derby.
rows.reference: He added it was "concerning" that Toyota UK had told the BBC that if Britain left the EU without a deal it would temporarily halt production at its factory in Burnaston, near Derby.

rows.source: "A nílò àdéhùn ìṣòwò,” Ọ̀gbẹ́ni Clark ló sọ bẹ́ẹ̀.
rows.output: "We need a trade agreement," Mr. Clark said.
rows.reference: "We need a deal," Mr Clark said.

rows.source: Aṣemọ́tò Jàpáàanù sọ pé ipa ààlà máa ṣe ìdádúró tí ó bá lọ jẹ́ pé kò sí àd’hpùn ìṣòwò Brexit lẹ́ mú kí ìpàdánù iṣẹ́ wà.
rows.output: The Japanese ambassador said that the impact of the border would be a barrier to trade, which would lead to a loss of jobs.
rows.reference: The Japanese carmaker said the impact of border delays in the event of a no-deal Brexit could cost jobs.

rows.source: Ẹ̀rọ̀ iṣẹ́ Burnaston - tí ó ń ṣe Toyota Auris àti Avensis - pèsè mọ́tò tó súnmọ́ 150,000 ní ọdún tó kọjá tí ó sì jẹ́ pé 90% ní wọ́n ṣàgbéjáde sí Ìṣọ̀kan Yúròpù tó kù.
rows.output: The Burnaston plant, which manufactures the Toyota Auris and Avensis, produced approximately 150,000 vehicles last year, with 90% of those exports to the rest of Europe.
rows.reference: The Burnaston plant - which makes Toyota's Auris and Avensis - produced nearly 150,000 cars last year of which 90% were exported to the rest of the European Union.

rows.source: "Ìwòyé mi ni pé tí Bírítéènì ba fi le jáde kúrò ní EU láìròtẹ́lẹ̀ ní òpin oṣù kẹta, ìgbéjáde máa dúró ní ilé iṣẹ́ wa,” Marvi Cooke ni ó sọ bẹ́ẹ̀, Alákòóso adarí ní Burnaston.
rows.output: "My view is that if Britain leaves the EU without a deal in March, production will stop at our factory," said Marvi Cooke, managing director at Burnaston.
rows.reference: "My view is that if Britain crashes out of the EU at the end of March we will see production stops in our factory," said Marvin Cooke, Toyota's managing director at Burnaston.

rows.source: Àwọn aṣemọ́tò UK tí fi ìjayà wọn hàn nípa fífi EU sílẹ̀ láìní àdéhùn lórí bí kíkọjá láàlà òkòwò ṣe máa ṣiṣẹ́, gẹ́gẹ́bí i Honda, BMW àti Jaguar Land Rover.
rows.output: UK carmakers are furious at being left out of the EU without a deal on how to keep the supply chain going, as Honda, BMW and Jaguar Land Rover have shown.
rows.reference: Other UK car manufacturers have raised fears about leaving the EU without agreement on how cross-border trade will function, including Honda, BMW and Jaguar Land Rover.

rows.source: BMW, fún àpẹẹrẹ, sọ pé ò máa ti Ẹ̀rọ iṣẹ́ kékeré rẹ̀ ní Oxford fún oṣù kan tí ó tẹ̀lé Brexit.
rows.output: For example, BMW said it would not produce the Mini in Oxford for a month following Brexit.
rows.reference: BMW, for example, says it will close its Mini plant in Oxford for a month following Brexit.

rows.source: Ohun ìkọminú jùlọ jẹ́mọ́ ohun tí àwọn aṣemọ́tò sọ pé ọ jẹ àwọń èwu ètò ìpèsè tí ó bá ṣẹlẹ̀ pé kò sí àdéhun ìṣòwò Brexit.
rows.output: The most striking thing about the technocrats' argument is that it is based on the assumption that there will be no trade agreement if Brexit occurs.
rows.reference: The main concerns relate to what carmakers say are supply chain risks in the event of a no-deal Brexit.

rows.source: Ìgbéjáde àtòpọ̀ Toyota dá lórí i “tó bá àkókò mu”, pẹ̀lú àwọn ẹ̀yà ara rẹ̀ tí ó ń wọlé ní gbogbo ìṣẹ́jú 37 láti ọ̀dọ̀ olùgbéjáde wọn ní UK àti EU fún àwọn mọ́tò láti tà jáde.
rows.output: The Toyota production system is based on "just in time", with its parts arriving every 37 seconds from its plants in the UK and EU for cars to be sold.
rows.reference: Toyota's production line is run on a "just-in-time" basis, with parts arriving every 37 minutes from suppliers in both the UK and the EU for cars made to order.

rows.source: Tí UK bá fi EU sílẹ̀ láìsí àdéhùn ìṣòwò ní 29 oṣù kẹta, ìdíwọ́ le wà ní ààlà ibode tí àwọn ilé iṣẹ́ sọ pé o le já sí ìdádúro àti àìnító àwọn ẹ̀yà ara.
rows.output: If the UK leaves the EU without a trade agreement on 29 March, there may be delays at the border which could lead to shortages and price increases, businesses have warned.
rows.reference: If the UK leaves the EU without a deal on 29 March, there could be disruption at the border which the industry says could lead to delays and shortages of parts.

rows.source: Kò ní ṣeéṣe fún Tòyótà láti ní ọjà nílẹ̀ tó ju ìwọ̀n ọjọ́ kan lọ ní ibi Ẹ̀rọ iṣẹ́ rẹ̀ ní Derbyshire, ilé iṣẹ́ náà ló sọ bẹ́ẹ̀, àtipé ìgbéṣẹ́jáde máa dáwọ́ dúró.
rows.output: It is impossible for Toyota to have a market presence of more than one day at its Derbyshire factory, the company said, adding that production will cease.
rows.reference: It would be impossible for Toyota to hold more than a day's worth of inventory at its Derbyshire plant, the company said, and so production would be stopped.

rows.source: Mr Clark sọ pé ète Theresa May fún ìbáṣepọ̀ ọjọ́ iwájú pẹ̀lú EU jẹ́ “àmọ̀ǹmọ̀ṣe láti yàgò fún àwọn àyẹ́wò ní ààlà ìbodè náà.”
rows.output: Mr. Clark said that Theresa May's plan for future relations with the EU is "a desperate attempt to avoid scrutiny at the border."
rows.reference: Mr Clark said Theresa May's Chequers plan for future relations with the EU is "precisely calibrated to avoid those checks at the border."

rows.source: "A nílò láti ní àdéhùn ìṣòwò. A nílò láti ní àdéhùn ìṣòwò tó dára jùlọ tí ó máa gbà wá láàyè bí mo ṣe sọ, tí kò kì í ṣe àṣeyọrí nìkán ní àkókò yì tí a lé gbàdún, ṣùgbọ́n fún wa láti má le sọ àǹfààní yìí nù,” ó sọ fún ètò rédíò 4 BBC Lónìí bẹ́ẹ̀.
rows.output: "We need a trade agreement. We need a better trade agreement that will allow us to live as I say, not just a success in the time we have been given, but to ensure that we do not lose this opportunity," he told BBC Radio 4's Today program.
rows.reference: "We need to have a deal. We want to have the best deal that will allow as I say not just the success at present to be enjoyed but for us to grasp this opportunity," he told BBC Radio 4's Today programme.

rows.source: "Ẹ̀rí àrídájú tí kìíṣe láti ọ̀dọ̀ Toyotà nìkan ṣùgbọ́n tí ó jẹ́ ti àwọn àṣemọ́tò jáde míràn ní pé a nílò láti rí dájú pé a tẹ̀síwájú nínú ohun tí a ti ńṣe láṣeyọrílórí àwọn ààtò ìpèsè.”
rows.output: "Unambiguous evidence from Toyota alone is not sufficient, but it is also from other manufacturers that we need to ensure that we continue to do what we have been doing well in terms of supply chain planning."
rows.reference: "The evidence from not just Toyota but other manufacturers is that we need to absolutely be able to continue what has been a highly successful set of supply chains."

rows.source: Toyota kò le sọ pàtò bí ó ṣe máa pẹ́ tó kí ìgbéṣẹ́jáde tó le dáwọ́ dúró, ṣùgbọ́n nígbà tí ó bá ṣe díẹ̀, ó kìlọ̀ pé àwọn ìṣùnà mìràn tó le jẹyọ máa ṣàdínkù ìledíje ẹ̀rọ ìṣẹ́ tí ó sì máa jásí ìpàdánù iṣẹ́.
rows.output: Toyota cannot specify how long the production stoppage will last, but when it does, it warns that other factors may reduce the competitiveness of the automotive industry and lead to job losses.
rows.reference: Toyota was unable to say how long production would be stopped, but in the longer term, warned that added costs would reduce the plant's competitiveness and eventually cost jobs.

rows.source: Peter Tsouvallaris, tí ó ti ṣiṣẹ́ ní Burnaston fún ọdún 24 tí ó sì jẹ́ adárí ìpàdé ìgbìmọ̀ òkòwò níibi ẹ̀rọ iṣẹ́ náà, sọ pé ó kàn àwọn ọmọ ẹgbẹ́ òun gan an: "Ní ìrírí mi, ní kété tí àwọn iṣẹ́ yìí bá lọ, wọ̀n kó ní padà wá mọ́ láeláee.
rows.output: Peter Tsouvallaris, who had worked at Burnaston for 24 years and was the head of the economic committee there, said that he had only been able to recruit a few members: "In my experience, as soon as these projects are finished, they immediately go back to their normal lives.
rows.reference: Peter Tsouvallaris, who has worked at Burnaston for 24 years and is the Unite union convenor at the plant, said his members are increasingly concerned: "In my experience once these jobs go they never come back.

rows.source: Agbẹnusọ fún ìjọba kan sọ wípé: "A ti taari èròǹgbà tí ó ṣe gẹ́gẹ́ tí ó ṣì mú ọgbọ́n wa fún ọjọ́ iwájú ìbáṣepọ̀ wa pẹ̀lú EU.”
rows.output: The government spokesman said: "We have been following the trend that is still in our favor for the future of our relationship with the EU."
rows.reference: A government spokesperson said: "We have put forward a precise and credible plan for our future relationship with the EU."

rows.source: Ìpàdé Trump pẹ̀lú Rosenstein lé ní ìdádúró lẹ́ẹ̀kan síi, Ilé Funfun Báláu ló sọ bẹ́ẹ̀.
rows.output: Trump's meeting with Rosenstein was delayed again, the White House said.
rows.reference: Trump meeting with Rosenstein may be delayed again, says White House

rows.source: Ìpàdé onípinnu-ńlá Donald Trump pẹ̀lú ìgbákejì àṣòfin gbogbogbò Rod Rosenstein le “sún síwájú fún ọ̀ṣẹ̀ kan mìíràn” bí ìjà lórí ẹnítí wọn dábàá fún ilé ẹjọ́ gíga Brett kavanaugh ṣe tẹ́ ṣíwájú, Ilé Funfun Báláú ló sọ bẹ́ẹ̀ ní Ọjọ́ ìsinmi.
rows.output: Donald Trump's high-stakes meeting with Deputy Attorney General Rod Rosenstein could "blow up in a week" if the fight over his nominee for the Supreme Court, Brett Kavanaugh, continues, White House press secretary Sarah Sanders said on Sunday.
rows.reference: Donald Trump's high-stakes meeting with deputy attorney general Rod Rosenstein could be "pushed back another week" as the fight over supreme court nominee Brett Kavanaugh continues, the White House said on Sunday.

rows.source: Rosensteinní ó ń ṣàbójútó iṣẹ́ àgbẹjọ́rò pàtàkì Robert Mueller, tí ó ń ṣe ìwádìí lórí i ìkọlù Rọ́ṣíà lórí ìdìbò, ìbáṣepọ̀ láàrin àwọn òṣiṣẹ́ Trump àti Rọ́ṣíà àti bí ó ṣe ṣẹéṣe sí fún ààrẹ láti dènà ètò ìdájọ tó péye.
rows.output: Rosenstein oversees the special counsel Robert Mueller's investigation, which is looking into Russian interference in the election, the connections between Trump's employees and Russia, and the possibility of the president obstructing the full investigation.
rows.reference: Rosenstein oversees the work of special counsel Robert Mueller, who is investigating Russian election interference, links between Trump aides and Russia and potential obstruction of justice by the president.

rows.source: Bóyá Trump máa dá igbákejì àṣòfin gbogbogbò dúró tàbí kò ní ṣe bẹ́ẹ̀, tí ó máa wá mú kí òmínira Mueller níra, ti jẹ́ kí Washington ṣòfófo fú ọ̀pọ̀ oṣù ṣẹ́yìn.
rows.output: Perhaps Trump will fire the special prosecutor or not, and that will force Mueller to resign, which has already caused Washington to be paralyzed for months.
rows.reference: Whether or not Trump will fire the deputy attorney general, and thereby endanger Mueller's independence, has fuelled Washington gossip for months.

rows.source: Ní ìbẹ̀rẹ̀ oṣù yìí, ìwé ìròyìn New York Times jábọ̀ pé Rosenstein jíròrò lórí i pé oùn fẹ́ fí wáyà sára láti ṣe àkásílẹ̀ ìtàkurọ̀sọ pẹ̀lú Trump àti ìṣeéṣesí láti yọ ààrẹ nínú àtúnṣe 25.
rows.output: At the beginning of this month, the New York Times reported that Rosenstein discussed the possibility of wearing a wire to record Trump and discussing the 25th Amendment.
rows.reference: Earlier this month, the New York Times reported that Rosenstein discussed wearing a wire to record conversations with Trump and the possibility of removing the president via the 25th amendment.

rows.source: Rosenstein ní ìròyìn yí kò rí bẹ́ẹ̀.
rows.output: Rosenstein said in a statement that he did not see it that way.
rows.reference: Rosenstein denied the report.

rows.source: Ṣùgbọ́n ní ọjọ́ ajé tó kọjá ó lọ sí Ilé Funfun Bbáláú, láàrin àwọn ìròyìn pé ó tí fẹ́ kswé fi ipò rẹ̀ sílẹ̀
rows.output: But on the day of the election, he went to the White House, amid reports that he had decided to step down from his position
rows.reference: But last Monday he went to the White House, amid reports he was about to resign.

rows.source: Dípò, ìpàdé pẹ̀lú Trump, ẹni tí ó wà ní ìpàdé Àjọ ìṣọ̀kan Àgbáyé ní New York ní àkókò náà, di kíkéde láti wáyé ní ọjọ́’rú.
rows.output: Instead, the meeting with Trump, who was at the United Nations General Assembly in New York at the time, was canceled.
rows.reference: Instead, a meeting with Trump, who was then at the United Nations in New York, was announced for Thursday.

rows.source: Trump sọ pé òun "kò ní fẹ́" láti dá Rosenstein dúró lẹ́nu iṣẹ́ ṣùgbọ́n lẹ́yìn èyí ìpàdé náà di dídá dúró díẹ̀ láti yàgò fún èdè àìyedè pẹ̀lú ìgbìmọ̀ ìdájọ́ Aṣòfin àgbà ní ibi tí Kavanaugh àti ọ̀kan lára àwọn obìnrin tí ó fi ẹ̀sùn ìbálòpọ̀ ní ọ́nà àìtọ́ kan Ọ̀mọ̀wé Christine Blassey Ford, àwọn méjèèjì ló jẹ́ ẹ̀rí
rows.output: Trump said he "doesn't want" to fire Rosenstein but the meeting was delayed to avoid controversy with the Senate Judiciary Committee, where Kavanaugh and one of the women accusing him of sexual misconduct, writer Christine Blasey Ford, were both testifying.
rows.reference: Trump said he would "prefer not" to fire Rosenstein but then the meeting was delayed to avoid a clash with the Senate judiciary committee hearing in which Kavanaugh and one of the women who have accused him of sexual misconduct, Dr Christine Blasey Ford, both testified.

rows.source: Ní ọjọ́ ẹtì, Trump pa àṣẹ fún FBI láti ṣe ìwádìí ẹ̀sùn tí wọ́n fi kan Kavanugh, tí ó tún mú kí ìdádúró wá fún píparí ìbò Ilé Aṣòfin àgbà.
rows.output: On the eve of the midterms, Trump ordered the FBI to investigate allegations against Kavanaugh, which also led to a delay in the confirmation vote of the Senate.
rows.reference: On Friday, Trump ordered a one-week FBI investigation of claims against Kavanaugh, further delaying a full Senate vote.

rows.source: Àkọ̀wé ìròyǹ Trump, Sarah Sanders, wà farahàn lórí ìòyìn Fox l’ọ́jọ́ Ìsinmi.
rows.output: Trump's former press secretary, Sarah Sanders, appeared on Fox News on Sunday.
rows.reference: Trump's press secretary, Sarah Sanders, appeared on Fox News Sunday.

rows.source: Nígbà tí wọ́n bèèrè ìpàdé pẹ̀lú Rosenstein, ó sọ pé: "A kò tíì ní déètì fún ìyẹn báyìí, ó le jẹ́ ọ̀ṣẹ̀ yìí, mó rí bí ìgbà pé ó máa sún ṣẹ́yìn fún ọ̀ṣẹ̀ míràn nítorí gbogbo nǹkan tí ó ń lọ lọ́wọ́ ní ilé ẹjọ́ tó ga jùlọ.
rows.output: When they asked for a meeting with Rosenstein, he said: "We don't have the information for that right now, it could be this week, or maybe the next week because everything is moving so fast in the highest court.
rows.reference: Asked about the Rosenstein meeting, she said: "A date for that hasn't been set, it could be this week, I could see that pushing back another week given all of the other things that are going on with the supreme court.

rows.source: Ṣùgbọ́n kí á máa wò bọ̀ àtipé mo máa ń fẹ́ fi ohun tí ó ńlọ tó àwọn oníròyìn létí.
