rows.reference: China's retaliatory tariffs early in the trade war were designed to hit exporters in states such as Iowa that supported Trump's Republican Party, Chinese and U.S. experts have said.

rows.source: Terry Branstad, onye nnọchite anya U.S na China bụkwa onye chịburu Iowa, onye mbupu ahịa nri ubi nke ukwuu na China, kwuru na China merụrụ ndị ọrụ, ndị ọrụ ugbo na azụmahịa nke America ahụ.
rows.output: Terry Branstad, the U.S. Ambassador to China and former governor of Iowa, which exports a lot of agricultural products to China, said that China has hurt American workers, farmers, and businesses.
rows.reference: Terry Branstad, the U.S. ambassador to China and the former longtime governor of Iowa, a major exporter of agricultural goods to China, said Beijing had hurt American workers, farmers and businesses.

rows.source: China, Branstad dere n’echiche ya na Des Moines Register na Sọnde, “na-ekwusi ike maka mmegide ahụ site na itinye mgbasa ozi n’akwụkwọ mgbasa ozi anyị.”
rows.output: China, Branstad wrote in his column for the Des Moines Register on Sunday, "emphasized the opposition by placing ads in our newspapers."
rows.reference: China, Branstad wrote in an opinion piece in Sunday's Des Moines Register, "is now doubling down on that bullying by running propaganda ads in our own free press."

rows.source: “N’ịgbasa ozi asị a, gọọmentị China na ewere oghere omenala America hụrụ n’anya bụ nke onye kwuo uche ya na mgbasa ozi enweghị mkpagbu were tinye mgbasa ozi akwụrụ ụgwọ na Des Moines Register.” Branstad dere.
rows.output: By disseminating this false information, the Chinese government is taking advantage of the cultural openness of the United States, which is a democratic country with a free press, to insert paid propaganda into the Des Moines Register.
rows.reference: "In disseminating its propaganda, China's government is availing itself of America's cherished tradition of free speech and a free press by placing a paid advertisement in the Des Moines Register," Branstad wrote.

rows.source: “Ma ịtụlee ya n’ọdụ akwụkwọ mgbasa ozi dị n’okporo beijing ebe a, ịga ahụ na enwere obere olu ndịiche nke na ịghaghị ahụ ihe n’egosi n’ezie echiche di iche ndị China nwere ike nwee maka usoro akụnụba China nọ na nsogbu, ebe ọ bụ n’ụlọ mgbasa ozi nọ na njikwa nke China Communist Party,” ọ dere.
rows.output: "But let's take a look at the media outlets in Beijing, where there is a small number of dissenting voices that are forced to show their true opinions on the Chinese Communist Party's economic policies, which are in crisis, as they are under the control of the Chinese Communist Party," he wrote.
rows.reference: "In contrast, at the newsstand down the street here in Beijing, you will find limited dissenting voices and will not see any true reflection of the disparate opinions that the Chinese people may have on China's troubling economic trajectory, given that media is under the firm thumb of the Chinese Communist Party," he wrote.

rows.source: Ọ gbakwunyere na “otu n’ime akwụkwọ akụkọ ama ama na China zenarịrị ibiputa” ederede ya, n’agbanyeghị na o kwughị akwụkwọ akụkọ nke ọ bụ.
rows.output: He also added that "one of the most popular Chinese news websites" published his article, even though he did not mention the news website.
rows.reference: He added that "one of China's most prominent newspapers dodged the offer to publish" his article, although he did not say which newspaper.

rows.source: Ndị Repọblikan Na-akpachapụ Ndị Ntuli Aka Ụmụ-nwanyị Tupu Ntuli Aka Ọkara Ọchịchị Maka Ọgbaghara Kavanaugh, Ndị Nyocha Dọrọ Aka na Ntị
rows.output: Republican Senators Block Women's Voting Rights Ahead of Kavanaugh Confirmation, Investigators Draw Attention
rows.reference: Republicans Alienating Women Voters Ahead of Midterms With Kavanaugh Debacle, Analysts Warn

rows.source: Dị ka ọtụtụ ndị isi Repọblikan kwụnyere ma kwuchitere Onye nhọpụta Ụlọ Ikpe Kachasị Elu Brett Kavanaugh n’ihu ebubo dị iche iche nke mmekọrịta nwoke na nwanyị, ndị nyocha adọọla aka na ntị na ha ga-ahụ ndapụta iwe ga-esite ọkachasị n’aka ụmụ-nwanyị, n’oge ntuli aka ọkara ọchịchị na-abịa.
rows.output: As many Republican leaders have stated and testified on behalf of Supreme Court nominee Brett Kavanaugh in the face of various accusations of sexual misconduct, investigators have warned that they will be looking for signs of heightened aggression particularly from women, in the upcoming midterm elections.
rows.reference: As many top Republicans stand-by and defend Supreme Court nominee Brett Kavanaugh in the face of several allegations of sexual assault, analyst have warned they will see a backlash, particularly from women, during the upcoming midterm elections.

rows.source: Mmetụta sochiri nke a dị elu nke ukwuu, na ọtụtụ ndị Repọblikan ka edekọbara na ha egosila na ha chọrọ ịga n’ihu mee ntuli aka.
rows.output: The consequences of this were so severe that many Republicans were recorded as having expressed that they wanted to go forward and make a vote.
rows.reference: The emotions surrounding this have been extremely high, and most Republicans are on record already showing they wanted to go forward with a vote.

rows.source: Enweghị ike iweghachi ihe ndị ahụ,” Grant Reeher, onye ọkammụta nke sayensị ndọrọndọrọ ọchịchị na Syracuse University Maxwell School gwara The Hill maka ederede nke ebiputara na Satọde.
rows.output: The Hill reported on Saturday that Grant Reeher, a political science professor at Syracuse University's Maxwell School, said, "It's not possible to restore the things that have been lost."
rows.reference: Those things can't be walked back," Grant Reeher, a professor of political science at Syracuse University's Maxwell School told The Hill for an article published Saturday.

rows.source: Reeher kwuru na ya na-agbagha n’ọkwụkwa ikpeazụ nke Onye Ọmebe Iwu Jeff Flake (R-Arizona) mere maka nyocha FBI a ga-ezu iji wetuo iwe ndị ntuli aka.
rows.output: Reeher said he was disappointed in the final vote of Senator Jeff Flake (R-Arizona) on the FBI's investigation to be conducted to address the concerns of the voters.
rows.reference: Reeher said he doubts Senator Jeff Flake's (R-Arizona) last-minute push for an FBI investigation will be enough to placate angry voters.

rows.source: “Ụmụ-nwanyị agaghị echefu ihe mere ụnyahụ - ha agaghị echefu echi niile ma Nọvemba, “ Karine Jean-Pierre, onye ndụmọdụ senịọ na onye nkwuchite okwu obodo maka otu ọganihu MoveOn kwuru na Fraịde, dabere na akwụkwọ akụkọ Washington, D.C.
rows.output: "Women will not forget what happened yesterday - they will not forget tomorrow and November, " Karine Jean-Pierre, a senior adviser and spokesperson for the progressive group MoveOn, said on Friday, based on a report in the Washington, D.C.
rows.reference: "Women are not going to forget what happened yesterday - they are not going to forget it tomorrow and not in November," Karine Jean-Pierre, a senior adviser and national spokeswoman for the progressive group MoveOn said on Friday, according to the Washington, D.C. newspaper.

rows.source: N’ụtụtụ Fraịde, ndị ngagharị iwe kwere ukwe “Nọvemba na-abịa!” ka ha na-agagharị ngagharị iwe n’ogologo ụzọ Nzụkọ Ọmeiwu ebe ndị Repọblikan ji Ọgbakọ Ọka Ikpe họrọ ịga n’ihu na nhọrọ Kavanaugh agbanyeghị nkwuputa Dr. Christine Blasey Ford, Mic kwuputara.
rows.output: On Friday morning, protesters chanted "November is coming!" as they marched through the streets of Capitol Hill where Republicans voted to advance Kavanaugh's nomination despite the testimony of Dr. Christine Blasey Ford, reported Mic.
rows.reference: On Friday morning, protestors chanted "November is coming!" as they demonstrated in the hallway of the Senate as the Republicans controlling the Judiciary Committee chose to move forward with Kavanaugh's nomination despite the testimony of Dr. Christine Blasey Ford, Mic reported.

rows.source: “Ịnụ ọkụ n’obi na mkpalite mmụọ nke Demokrat ga-apụ iche,” Stu Rothenberg, onye nyocha ndọrọndọrọ ọchịchị enweghị otu o binyere gwara ndị akụkọ.
rows.output: "Fire in the belly and the soul of the Democrat will be different," Stu Rothenberg, a nonpartisan political analyst, told reporters.
rows.reference: "Democratic enthusiasm and motivation is going to be off the chart," Stu Rothenberg, a nonpartisan political analyst, told the news site.

rows.source: “Ndị mmadụ na-ekwu na ọ dịla elu; nke a bụ eziokwu.
rows.output: "People say it's already high; this is true."
rows.reference: "People are saying it's already been high; that's true.

rows.source: Mana ọ nwere ike ịgbagokwu ọkachasị n’etiti ụmụ-nwanyị n’enweghị otu ha binyere n’ime obodo yana ndị ntuli aka na-etolite etolite, gbara afọ 18- ruo 29-, bụ ndị ebe onye isi ala anaghị amasị, anaghị eme ntuli aka kwa mgbe.”
rows.output: But it can be especially pronounced among women in rural areas, where there is no consensus among the electorate, and among young voters, aged 18 to 29, who are generally unenthusiastic about the president.
rows.reference: But it could be higher, particularly among swing women voters in the suburbs and younger voters, 18- to 29-year-olds, who while they don't like the president, often don't vote."

rows.source: Ọbụlagodi tupu nkwuputanke ọha Ford mere na-akọwa ebubo mmekọrịta nwoke na nwanyị megide onye nhọpụta Ụlọ Ikpe kachasị Elu, ndị nyocha na-atụ elo na ndapụta iwe nwere ike sote ma ọ bụrụ na ndị Repọblikan gaa n’ihu mee nkwado ahụ.
rows.output: Before Ford's public statement, the investigators were speculating that the fallout from the allegations of sexual misconduct against the Supreme Court nominee could be even worse if Republicans proceeded with the confirmation vote.
rows.reference: Even before Ford's public testimony detailing her allegations of sexual assault against the Supreme Court nominee, analysts suggested a backlash could follow if Republicans pushed forward with the confirmation.

rows.source: “Nke a abụrụla ọgbaghara dịịrị GOP,” Michael Steele kwuru, onye isi chịburu Ọgbakọ Otu Repọblikan, na mbido izug ara aga, dabere na NBC News.
rows.output: "This has been a disaster for the GOP," said Michael Steele, former chairman of the Republican National Committee, in an interview with NBC News.
rows.reference: "This has become a muddled mess for the GOP," said Michael Steele, former chairman of the Republican National Committee, early last week, according to NBC News.

rows.source: “Ọ bụghị naanị maka ntuli aka ndị ọgbakọ ma ọ bụ maka ntuli aka ikpeazụ ma ọ bụ ma etinyere Kavanaugh n’oche, ọ bụkwa maka otu ndị Repọblikan siri jikwaa ihe a ma ka ha siri meso ya omume,” Guy Cecil, onye isi Priorities USA, otu na-enyere aka ahọpụta ndị Demokrat, rụtụrụ ndị akụkọ aka.
rows.output: “It’s not just about the House races or the Senate races or whether Kavanaugh is on the court, it’s about how the Republicans are handling this and how they’re going to use it,” Guy Cecil, the chairman of Priorities USA, a group that helps elect Democrats, told reporters.
rows.reference: "It's just not about the committee vote or the final vote or whether Kavanaugh is put on the bench, it's also about the way Republicans have handled this and how they have treated her," Guy Cecil, director of Priorities USA, a group that helps to elect Democrats, pointed out to the news channel.

rows.source: Kaosiladị, Ndị America dị ka ndị kewara ekewa n’onye ha ga-ekwenyere na ndapụta nkwuputa Ford na Kavanaugh, ebe ndị karịrị kwụnyere onye nke ikpeazụ.
rows.output: However, Americans are divided on whether to trust Ford's testimony and Kavanaugh's confirmation.
rows.reference: However, Americans appear to be somewhat split over who to believe in the wake of Ford's and Kavanaugh's testimonies, with slightly more siding with the latter.

rows.source: Nyocha ọhụrụ sitere na YouGov gosiri na pesentị 41 ndị zara ajụjụ kwenyere kpamkpam ma ọ bụ kwenyetụrụ nkwuputa Ford, ebe pesentị 35 kwuru na ha kwenyere kpamkpam ma ọ bụ kwenyetụrụ Kavanaugh.
rows.output: A new survey from YouGov shows that 41% of respondents completely agree or somewhat agree with Ford's statement, while 35% completely agree or somewhat agree with Kavanaugh's statement.
rows.reference: A new poll from YouGov shows that 41 percent of respondents definitely or probably believed Ford's testimony, while 35 percent said they definitely or probably believed Kavanaugh.

rows.source: Na mgbakwunye, pesentị 38 kwuru na ha chere na Kavanaugh eleghị anya sịrị asị ma ọ bụ sịa asị kpamkpam n’oge nkwuputa ya, ebe naanị pesentị 30 kwuru otu ihe ahụ maka Ford.
rows.output: In addition, 38 percent said they believed that Kavanaugh was probably lying or completely lying during his testimony, while only 30 percent said the same about Ford.
rows.reference: Additionally, 38 percent said they thought Kavanaugh has probably or definitely lied during his testimony, while just 30 percent said the same about Ford.

rows.source: Ka Flake mechara nkwanye, ndị FBI na-eme nyocha ugbu a n’ebubo Ford boro, yana opekempe otu onye ebubo ọzọ, Deborah Ramirez mere, The Guardian kwuputara.
rows.output: After Flake's acquittal, the FBI is currently investigating Ford's accusations, as well as at least one other accusation, Deborah Ramirez, The Guardian reported.
rows.reference: After the push from Flake, the FBI is currently investigating the allegations brought forward by Ford as well as at least one other accuser, Deborah Ramirez, The Guardian reported.

rows.source: Ford mere nkwuputa n’ihu Ọgbakọ Ndị Ikpe Nzụkọ Ọmeiwu n’okpuru iyi n’izu gara aga na Kavanaugh dakporo ya n’anya mmanya mgbe ọ gbara afọ 17.
rows.output: Ford made a statement before the House Judiciary Committee under oath last week that Kavanaugh assaulted her when she was 17 years old.
rows.reference: Ford testified before the Senate Judiciary Committee under oath last week that Kavanaugh drunkenly assaulted her at the age of 17.

rows.source: Ramirez boro ebubo n’onye nhọpụta Ụlọ Ikpe Kachasị Elu ahụ gosiri ya ike ya mgbe ha na-eme ọgbakọ oriri na ọṅụṅụ n’oge ha na-agụ akwụkwọ na Yale n’ime 1980s.
rows.output: Ramirez was accused by the nominee to the Supreme Court of showing off his wealth when they were attending a cocktail party during their studies at Yale in the 1980s.
rows.reference: Ramirez alleges that the Supreme Court nominee exposed his genitals to her while they attended a party during their time studying at Yale in the 1980s.

rows.source: Onye Mmepụta World Wide Web Na-ama Atụmatụ Ịmalite Ịntanetị Ọhụrụ Iji Sonyere Google na Facebook
rows.output: The World Wide Web Inventor Announces Plan to Launch New Internet Network to Compete with Google and Facebook
rows.reference: The Inventor of the World Wide Web Plans to Start a New Internet to Take on Google and Facebook

rows.source: Tim Berners-Lee, onye mmepụta World Wide Web, na-amalite ụlọ ọrụ ọhụrụ nke ga-achụso Facebook, Amazon na Google.
rows.output: Tim Berners-Lee, the inventor of the World Wide Web, is starting a new company that will compete with Facebook, Amazon, and Google.
rows.reference: Tim Berners-Lee, the inventor of the World Wide Web, is launching a startup that seeks to rival Facebook, Amazon and Google.

rows.source: Atụmatụ ọhụrụ ahụ nke ọkaibe teknụzụ, Inrupt, bụ ụlọ ọrụ na-agbakwasa ụkwụ na ngwanro ghe oghe Berners-Lee, Solid.
rows.output: The new plan, Inrupt, is a startup that is building on top of Berners-Lee's open-source software, Solid.
rows.reference: The technology legend's latest project, Inrupt, is a company that builds off of Berners-Lee's open source platform Solid.

rows.source: Solid na-enye ndị ọrụ oghere ịhọrọ ebe ha ga-echekwa data ha yana ozi ndị mmadụ nwere ike nweta.
rows.output: Solid provides users with the opportunity to choose where they store their data and the information that people can access.
rows.reference: Solid allows users to choose where their data is stored and what people are allowed to have access to what information.

rows.source: N’ajụjụ ọnụ pụrụ iche Fast Company mere, Berners-Lee mara njakịrị na ebumnuche ejiri mebe Inrupt bụ “ịchị mba ụwa.”
rows.output: In a special interview with Fast Company, Berners-Lee joked that the purpose of Inrupt was "to take over the world."
rows.reference: In an exclusive interview with Fast Company, Berners-Lee joked that the intent behind Inrupt is "world domination."

rows.source: “Anyị ga-eme ya ugbu a,” o kwuru maka ụlọ ọhụrụ ahụ.
rows.output: "We will do it now," he said for the new building.
rows.reference: "We have to do it now," he said of the startup.

rows.source: “Ọ bụ oge a ga-edebanye na akụkọ.”
rows.output: "It's time to put our mark on history."
rows.reference: "It's a historical moment."

rows.source: Ngwa ahụ na-eji teknụzụ Solid enye ndị mmadụ oghere imepụta “ebe nchekwa data nkeonwe n’ịntanetị” ma ọ bụ POD.
rows.output: The tool uses Solid technology to give people space to create their own "private data storage space on the internet" or POD.
rows.reference: The app uses Solid's technology to allow people to create their own "personal online data store" or a POD.

rows.source: Ọ nwere ike inwe ndepụta kọntaktị, ndepụta ihe omume, kalenda, ọba egwu yana ngwa nkeonwe na nke eji arụ ọrụ.
rows.output: It may have a list of contacts, a list of tasks, a calendar, a music library, and personal and work apps.
rows.reference: It can contain contact lists, to-do lists, calendar, music library and other personal and professional tools.

rows.source: Ọ dị ka Google Drive, Microsoft Outlook, Slack na Spotify dị n’otu nchọgharị ma ha niile n’otu oge.
rows.output: It's like Google Drive, Microsoft Outlook, Slack, and Spotify all in one search and all at once.
rows.reference: It's like Google Drive, Microsoft Outlook, Slack and Spotify are all available on one browser and all at the same time.

rows.source: Ihe pụrụ iche na ebe nchekwa data nkeonwe n’ịntanetị bụ na ọ dịịrị naanị onye ji ya arụ ọrụ ịhọrọ onye ga-enweta ozi nke ọ bụla.
rows.output: The unique thing about private data storage on the internet is that it is up to the person who owns it to decide who gets to access their information.
rows.reference: What's unique about the personal online data store is that it is completely up to the user who can access what kind of information.

rows.source: Ụlọ ọrụ ahụ na-akpọ ya “ikike nkeonwe site na data.”
rows.output: The company calls it "private power from data."
rows.reference: The company calls it "personal empowerment through data."

rows.source: Ebumnuche Inrupt, dabere na CEO John Bruce, bụ ka ụlọ ọrụ kpokọba, akụrụngwa, usoro na nka dabara daba iji nyere aka mee ka Solid rute onye ọ bụla.
rows.output: Inrupt's mission, based on CEO John Bruce, is to bring together companies, technologies, systems, and skills to help make Solid accessible to everyone.
rows.reference: The idea for Inrupt, according to the company's CEO John Bruce, is for the company to bring resources, process and appropriate skills to help make Solid available to everyone.

rows.source: Ụlọ ọrụ ahụ nwere naanị Berners-Lee, Bruce, ebe nchekwa IBM zụtara na ya, ndị ọrụ nrụpụta ewere n’ọrụ ịrụ n’atụmatụ ahụ yana ọgbakọ ndị koodu wepụtara onwe ha.
rows.output: The company had only Berners-Lee, Bruce, where IBM's storage division had purchased it, and the production staff who were hired to work on the project, as well as a group of volunteer coders.
rows.reference: The company currently consists of Berners-Lee, Bruce, a security platform bought by IBM, some on-staff developers contracted to work on the project, and a community of volunteer coders.

rows.source: Site n’izu a, ndị nrụpụta teknụzụ ụwa gbaa gburugburu ga-enwe ike mebe ngwa agaghị ekpokọba ọnụ nke ha site n’iji ngwa mebere na websaịtị Inrupt.
rows.output: By the end of this year, global tech manufacturers will be able to create non-invasive devices using the open-source software developed by Inrupt.
rows.reference: Starting this week, technology developers around the world could create their own decentralized apps using the tools available on the Inrupt website.

rows.source: Berners-Lee kwuru na ya ndị otu ya anaghị agwa ndị “Facebook na Google okwu banyere ma ha a ga-amalite ma ọ bụ hapụ mmalite mgbanwe kpamkpam ebe ụdịdị azụmahịa na-atụgharị ozugbo na ntabi anya.
rows.output: Berners-Lee said that his team was not talking to "Facebook and Google about whether they would start or leave the initiative completely, where the commercial models were turning immediately to the attention of the public."
rows.reference: Berners-Lee said that he and his team are not talking to "Facebook and Google about whether or not to introduce a complete change where all their business models are completely upended overnight.

rows.source: “Anyị anaghị anata ha ikike.”
rows.output: "We do not accept them."
rows.reference: "We are not asking their permission."

rows.source: Na mbipụta emere na Medium na Satọde, Berners-Lee dere na “ebumnuche Inrupt bụ inye ike azụmahịa na gburugburu inyere aka chekwaa ntụkwasị obi na ịdị mma weebu ọhụrụ ahụ arụrụ na Solid.”
rows.output: In a Medium post published on Saturday, Berners-Lee wrote that "Inrupt's goal is to empower businesses to create a sustainable, trustworthy, and decentralized web."
rows.reference: In a post on Medium published on Saturday, Berners-Lee wrote that Inrupt's "mission is to provide commercial energy and an ecosystem to help protect the integrity and quality of the new web built on Solid."

rows.source: Na 1994, Berners-Lee gbanwere Ịntanetị mgbe ọ mepụtara World Wide Web Consortuim na Massachusetts Institue of Technology.
rows.output: In 1994, Berners-Lee revolutionized the Internet by creating the World Wide Web Consortium at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.
rows.reference: In 1994, Berners-Lee transformed the Internet when he established the World Wide Web Consortium at Massachusetts Institute of Technology.

rows.source: N’ọnwa ndị adịbeghị anya, Berners-Lee bụ olu na-ada ụda na arụmarụ ụka nnwere onwe ọrụ ịntanetị.
rows.output: In recent months, Berners-Lee has been a vocal advocate for the freedom of the internet.
rows.reference: In recent months, Berners-Lee has been an influential voice in the net neutrality debate.

rows.source: Ọbulagodi mgbe a na-ebuputa Inrupt, Berners-Lee ga-anọrọ dịka onye Mmepụta na Onye Isi nke World Wide Web Consortuim, Web Foundation na Open Data Institute.
rows.output: Even after leaving the W3C, Berners-Lee remained as the Technical Director and Chief Architect of the World Wide Web Consortium, Web Foundation, and Open Data Institute.
rows.reference: Even while launching Inrupt, Berners-Lee will remain the Founder and Director of World Wide Web Consortium, the Web Foundation and the Open Data Institute.

rows.source: “A na m enwe olile anya nke ukwuu maka oge na-abịa n’ihu nke weebu,” Berners-Lee gbakwunyere.
rows.output: "I am very excited about the future of the web," Berners-Lee added.
rows.reference: "I'm incredibly optimistic for this next era of the web," Berners-Lee added.

rows.source: Bernard Vann: Emere emume onye ụkọchukwu Victoria Cross WW1
rows.output: Bernard Vann: A memorial service for the WW1 Victoria Cross priest
rows.reference: Bernard Vann: WW1 Victoria Cross cleric celebrated

rows.source: Emeela emume nke naanị ụkọchukwu Church of England nwetara mmeri Victoria Cross n’oge World War One dị ka onye agha n’obodo ya ka afọ gbara 100.
rows.output: The Church of England has held a service to honor the only Victoria Cross recipient from the local community during World War One, 100 years after his death.
rows.reference: The only Church of England cleric to win a Victoria Cross during World War One as a combatant has been celebrated in his hometown 100 years on.

rows.source: Lt Col Ụkọchukwu Bernard Vann nwetara awọdụ na 29, Septemba 1918 na mbuso agha emere na Bellenglise na Lehaucourt.
rows.output: Lt Col Uko Bernard Vann was awarded the Distinguished Service Order on 29 September 1918 for the attack on Bellenglise and Lehaucourt.
rows.reference: Lt Col The Reverend Bernard Vann won the award on 29 September 1918 in the attack at Bellenglise and Lehaucourt.

rows.source: Kaosiladị, mgbọ ọkaibe n’ịgba egbe tụrụ ya ka ụbọchị anọ gachara na ọ maghị ncha ncha na etubere ya ugo ndị agha kachasị na Britain.
rows.output: However, a remarkable shot in the shooting competition threw him off balance four days later, and he did not know how to handle the honor of being the best soldier in Britain.
rows.reference: However, he was killed by a sniper four days later and never knew he had won the highest British military honour.

rows.source: Ụmụ ụmụ ya ndị nwoke abụọ kpughere okwute iji na-eme ncheta ya na ngarube emere na Rushden, Northamptonshire, na Satọde.
rows.output: His two grandsons unveiled a stone to commemorate him at a memorial service held in Rushden, Northamptonshire, on Saturday.
rows.reference: A commemorative stone was unveiled by his two grandsons at a parade in Rushden, Northamptonshire, on Saturday.

rows.source: Otu n’ime nwa nwa ya Michael Vann, kwuru na ọ bụ “ihe nrịbama pụrụ iche nke ukwuu” na a ga-ekpughe okwute ahụ ka afọ gbara 100 kpọmkwem site na mgbe nna ya ochie kpara ike o jiri nweta awọdụ.

rows.source: Ndị ọzụzụ na ndị ahụike nyere Abercrombie oxygen n’akụkụ ahụ tupu edowe ya n’ihe ndọkpụrụ wee buru ya laghachi maka nyocha ndị ọzọ.
rows.output: The trainers and healthcare providers administered oxygen to Abercrombie's side before placing him in a splint and transporting him for further evaluation.
rows.reference: Trainers and medical personnel gave Abercrombie oxygen on the sideline before placing him on a stretcher and taking him back for further evaluation.

rows.source: Otu onye ọrụ si na Tennessee State gwara Chris Harris nke WSMV dị na Nashville, Tennessee, na Abercrombie apụtala n’ụlọ ịwa ahụ na Vanderbilt Medical Center.
rows.output: A worker from Tennessee State told Chris Harris of WSMV in Nashville, Tennessee, that Abercrombie appeared in the hospital at Vanderbilt Medical Center.

rows.source: Harris tinyere na “enwebeghị nkọwapụta n’ụdịrị/ogo nke ahụ mmerụ ahụ” na ndị Tennessee State na anwa ịmata mgbe ahụ mmerụ ahụ mere.
rows.output: Harris said, "There's no clarity in the form/degree of the injury" with Tennessee State and trying to figure out when the injury occurred.

rows.source: Abercrombie, onye nke abụọ na kọleji na eyi uwe ọbara ọbara, nọ n’afọ nke izizi ya na Tennessee State ka o sichara Illinois gafete.
rows.output: Abercrombie, the second in college and wearing a red shirt, was in his first year at Tennessee State after walking off the field in Illinois.

rows.source: Ọ nwere mgbakọta mgbochi ise na Satọde tupu ọ pụọ n’egwuregwu ahụ, nke wetere mgbakọ afọ asọmpi ya na mgbochi 18.
rows.output: He has five defensive tackles on Saturday before leaving the game, which brought his season total to 18 defensive tackles.
rows.reference: He had five total tackles Saturday before exiting the game, which brought his season total to 18 tackles.

rows.source: A ga-agba ndị azụmahịa ofesi ụgwọ ọrụ stampụ ka dị elu mgbe ha zụtara akụ n’ime UK
rows.output: Foreign businesses will be charged a higher stamp duty when purchasing assets in the UK
rows.reference: Foreign buyers will be charged higher stamp duty when they buy a property in the UK

rows.source: A ga-agba ndị azụmahịa ofesi ụgwọ ọrụ stampụ ka dị elu mgbe ha zụtara akụ n’ime UK ma jiri ego ahụ mara n’elu wee nyere ndị na enweghị ụlọ aka n’okpuru atụmatụ Tory
rows.output: Businesses abroad will be charged higher stamp duty when buying UK assets and the revenue will be used to help those without a home under the Tory plan.
rows.reference: Foreign buyers will be charged higher stamp duty when they buy a property in the UK with the extra cash used to help the homeless under new Tory plans

rows.source: Omume ahụ ga-emebi ọganihu nke agbamume Corbyn ịdọta ndị ntuli aka na etolite
rows.output: The move will undermine the progress made by Corbyn in attracting voters and building support.

rows.output: The cost of stamp duty relief will be charged to the account of non-resident buyers in the UK.
rows.reference: The stamp duty rise will be levied on those who are not paying tax in the UK

rows.source: Ụlọ Akụ na atụ anya ka ọ gbagote nde £120 kwa afọ - iji nyere ndị na enweghị ụlọ aka
rows.output: The Bank of Mum is expected to grow by £120 million a year - to help those without a home.
rows.reference: The Treasury expects it raise up to £120 million a year- to help the homeless

rows.source: A na achọ ịgba ndị azụmahịa ofesi ụgwọ ọrụ stampụ dị elu mgbe ha zụtara akụ n’ime UK - a ga-eji ego mara n’elu wee nyere ndị na enweghị ụlọ aka, Theresa May ga-ekwupute nke a taa.
rows.output: We are demanding that foreign businesses pay higher stamp duty when they buy assets in the UK - the money will be used to help those without a home, Theresa May will announce this today.
rows.reference: Foreign buyers are set to be charged a higher stamp duty rate when they buy property in the UK - with the extra cash used to help the homeless, Theresa May will announce today.

rows.source: A ga-ahụta nke ahụ ka ọnwụnwa iji mebie ọganihu nke agbamume Jeremy Corbyn iji dọta ndị ntuli aka na etolite eto site na iji nkwa ịnyekwu ụlọ dị ọnụ ala ma chụwa ndị na erite nnukwu ụgwọ ọnwa.
rows.output: That would be seen as a betrayal to undermine the progress of Jeremy Corbyn's campaign to attract voters by promising to build more affordable housing and to sack those on high salaries.
rows.reference: The move will be seen as an attempt to neutralise the success of Jeremy Corbyn's drive to attract young voters with pledges to provide more affordable housing and target high earners.

rows.source: A ga-agba ụgwọ ọrụ stampụ n’isi ndị mmadụ na ụlọ ọrụ ndị na anaghị akwụ ụgwọ ụtụ isi na UK, ego mara n’elu ga-ebuwanye mbọ Gọọmentị iji luso enweghị ụlọ agha.
rows.output: A tax on stamp duty will be levied on individuals and companies that do not pay corporation tax in the UK, with the revenue used to increase the Government's efforts to combat tax avoidance.
rows.reference: The stamp duty rise will be levied on individuals and firms not paying tax in the UK, with the extra money boosting the Government's drive to combat rough sleeping.

rows.source: Mgbakwunye ụgwọ ahụ - nke bụ mgbakwunye n’ọrụ stampụ dị ugbu a, gụnyere ọkwa ndị dị elu ebubatara n’afọ abụọ gara aga n’ụlọ nke abụọ yana ịzụta-maka-ịgbazinye - nwere ike irucha pasentị atọ.
rows.output: The additional tax - which is an addition to the current stamp duty, including higher rates introduced two years ago in the second house and the purchase-for-lease option - could reach three percent.
rows.reference: The surcharge - which is in addition to the present stamp duty, including the higher levels introduced two years ago on second homes and buy-to-lets - could be as much as three per cent.

rows.source: Ụlọ Akụ na atụ anya ka ọ gbagote nde £120 kwa afọ.
rows.output: The Bank is expected to rise by £120 million per year.

rows.source: Ekpebiri na pasentị 13 bụ ndị na abụghị ndị bi na UK na azụta akụ ndị London arụrụ ọhụrụ, na ebugo ụgwọ ma na eme ka o sie ike maka ndị na eme nzụta izizi ha iji nweta ọganihu n’nzọụkwụ obibi ụlọ.
rows.output: The government has decided that 13 percent of the population are not UK residents and are purchasing new-build London properties, and that they are paying taxes and making it difficult for first-time buyers to achieve progress in the housing market.
rows.reference: An estimated 13 per cent of new-build London properties are bought by non-UK residents, driving up prices and making it harder for first-time buyers to get a foot on the housing ladder.

rows.source: Imirikiti mpaghara ndị nwere ego n’obodo ahụ - karịchara n’isi ala - nwere “ime obodo tọgbọ nkịtị” n’ihi ọnụọgụ nke ndị nzụta ofesi dị elu, ndị na anọ ọtụtụ oge ha na mpụga nke obodo ahụ.
rows.output: The local elites in the country - especially in the capital - have "immigrant communities" because of the high number of foreign residents, who often spend most of their time outside the city.
rows.reference: Many wealthy areas of the country - particularly in the capital - have become "ghost towns" because of the high number of foreign buyers who spend most of their time out of the country.

rows.source: Iwu ọhụrụ ahụ na abịa n’izu ole ma ole ka Boris Johnson kpọchara oku maka mgbubi n’ọrụ stampụ iji nyere ndị ntorobịa aka ịnwe ụlọ izizi nke ha.
rows.output: The new law is set to come into force in a matter of weeks after Boris Johnson called for a stamp duty holiday to help young people buy their first home.
rows.reference: The new policy comes just weeks after Boris Johnson called for a stamp duty cut to help more young people own their first home.

rows.source: O boro ndị nnukwu ụlọ ọrụ nrụpụta ebubo maka idowe akụ n’ọnụego dị elu site na ịnapụ ala mana ha anaghị eji ya, ma rịọ Nwada May ka ọ hapụ oke n’ụlọ ndị dị ọnụ ala iji dozie “ihere ụlọ obibi” nke Britain.
rows.output: He accused large manufacturing companies of hoarding land at high prices by not using it, and asked Mrs. May to relax the limits on affordable housing to address the "housing shame" of Britain.
rows.reference: He accused big construction firms of keeping property prices high by snapping up land but not using it, and urged Mrs May to abandon quotas on affordable homes to fix Britain's "housing disgrace."

rows.source: Maazị Corbyn ekwuputela usoro mmezi ụlọ obibi na adọta ntinye uche, gụnyere njikwa ụgwọ ụlọ yana nkwụsị nke nchụpụ “abụghị ụta mmadụ”.
rows.output: Mr. Corbyn has announced a series of housing repair measures and attracting attention, including rent control and the abolition of "no-fault" evictions.
rows.reference: Mr Corbyn has announced an eye-catching series of proposed housing reforms, including rent controls and an end to "no-fault" evictions.

rows.source: Ọ chọkwara ịnyekwu ndị kansụl ikike iji rụpụta ụlọ ọhụrụ.
rows.output: He wanted to give the council more power to build new homes.
rows.reference: He also wants to give councils greater powers to build new homes.

rows.source: Nwada May kwuru: “Afọ gara aga m kwuru m ga-ewepụta ọchịchị m iji weghachite nrọ Britain - ndụ ahụ kwesịrị ka mma maka agbụrụ ọhụrụ ọ bụla.
rows.output: Ms. May said: "Last year I said I would remove my government to restore the British dream - life should be better for any new generation.
rows.reference: Mrs May said: "Last year I said I would dedicate my premiership to restoring the British dream - that life should be better for each new generation.

rows.source: Ma nke ahụ pụtara idozi ahịa ụlọ obibi anyị mebiri emebi.
rows.output: But that means fixing our broken housing market.
rows.reference: And that means fixing our broken housing market.

rows.source: Britain ga-ekpughere oge niile maka ndị mmadụ chọrọ ibi, rụọ ọrụ ma bido ndụ ebe a.
rows.output: Britain will be open to all those who want to live, work and start a life here.
rows.reference: Britain will always be open to people who want to live, work and build a life here.

rows.source: Kaosiladị, ọ nweghị ike ịdị mma na ọ dị mfe maka ndị mmadụ na ebighi n’ime UK, yanakwa ụlọ ọrụ ndị ofesi, iji zụta ụlọ ka ndị obibi Britain na arụsị ọrụ ike.
rows.output: However, it is not possible to be fair and easy for people and foreign companies to buy homes when British citizens are struggling to afford them.
rows.reference: However, it cannot be right that it is as easy for individuals who don't live in the UK, as well as foreign-based companies, to buy homes as hard-working British residents.

rows.source: Maka ọtụtụ ndị mmadụ, nrọ nke ịnwe ụlọ nke ha bụzị ihe ọ nọ nso eru aka, mmetọ nke enweghị ebe obibi bụzị ihe dị ire.”
rows.output: For many people, the dream of owning their own home is just out of reach, the lack of affordable housing is a nightmare.
rows.reference: For too many people the dream of home ownership has become all too distant, and the indignity of rough sleeping remains all too real."

rows.source: Jack Ross: ‘Ọchịchọ m kachasị bụ ijikwa Scotland’
rows.output: Jack Ross: 'My greatest wish is to manage Scotland'
rows.reference: Jack Ross: 'My ultimate ambition is to manage Scotland'

rows.source: Onye isi nke Sunderland Jack Ross kwuru na “ọchịchọ ya kachasị” bụ ịbụrụ onye ndu Scotland otu oge.
rows.output: Sunderland's manager Jack Ross said his "biggest wish" was to be Scotland's manager one day.
rows.reference: Sunderland boss Jack Ross says his "ultimate ambition" is to become the Scotland manager at some stage.

rows.source: Onye Scotland ahụ, 42, na enwe obi ụtọ maka mgba nke iweghachite otu asọmpi North-East, ndị nọ ugbu a n’ọkwa atọ na League One, akara atọ n’okpuru nke isi.
rows.output: The 42-year-old Scot is delighted with the challenge of trying to bring the North-East title back, with the current holders, who are currently third in League One, three points clear of the top.
rows.reference: The Scot, 42, is relishing the challenge of reviving the North-East club, who currently sit third place in League One, three points off the top.

rows.source: Ọ gara na Stadium of Light n’ọkọchị a ka o duchara St Mirren laghachite na Scottish Premiership n’afọ asọmpi gara aga.
rows.output: He went to the Stadium of Light on Saturday to lead St Mirren back to the Scottish Premiership in the previous season's campaign.
rows.reference: He moved to the Stadium of Light this summer after guiding St Mirren back to the Scottish Premiership last season.

rows.source: “Achọburu m ịgbara obodo m bọọlụ ka m bụ onye egwu.
rows.output: I wanted to play football for my country as a player.
rows.reference: "I wanted to play for my country as a player.

rows.source: Enwetara m cap B nke ahụ bụ ya,” Ross gwara Sportsound nke BBC Scotland.
rows.output: I got that B cap, and that was it," Ross told Sportsound of BBC Scotland.
rows.reference: I got a B cap and that was it," Ross told BBC Scotland's Sportsound.

rows.source: “Mana etolitere m na elele Scotland na Hampden ọtụtụ oge, mụ na nna m ka m bụ nwata, ọ bụ ihe na adọghachi m oge niile.
rows.output: But I grew up watching Scotland play at Hampden many times, with my father when I was a kid, and it's something that has always stuck with me.
rows.reference: "But I grew up watching Scotland at Hampden a lot with my dad as a kid, and it is always something that has drawn me back.

rows.source: Ohere ahụ ga-abịa, agbanyeghị, ọ bụrụ na m mee nke ọma na njikwa otu egwuregwu.”
rows.output: The opportunity will come, however, if I do well in managing the team.
rows.reference: That opportunity would only come, though, if I am successful in club management."

rows.source: Ndị bịara tupu Ross ka onye ndu Sunderland gụnyere Dick Advocaat, David Moyes, Sam Allardyce, Martin O'Neill, Roy Keane, Gue Poyet na Paulo Di Canio.
rows.output: The previous managers of Sunderland before Ross included Dick Advocaat, David Moyes, Sam Allardyce, Martin O'Neill, Roy Keane, Gue Poyet, and Paulo Di Canio.
rows.reference: Ross's predecessors as Sunderland manager include Dick Advocaat, David Moyes, Sam Allardyce, Martin O'Neill, Roy Keane, Gus Poyet and Paulo Di Canio.

rows.source: Onye isi nke Alloa Athletic gara aga kwuru na ọ naghị enwe ụjọ n’isochi aha ndị ahụ ama ama n’ụdịrị nnukwu otu ahụ, ka ọ jụchara arịrịọ ndị si na Barnsley na Ipswich Town.
rows.output: The former chairman of Alloa Athletic said he was not afraid to follow in the footsteps of the famous names in the big club's style, as he rejected requests from Barnsley and Ipswich Town.
rows.reference: The former Alloa Athletic boss says he felt no trepidation in following such established names at such a big club, having previously rejected overtures from Barnsley and Ipswich Town.

rows.source: “Ọganihu maka m n’oge a ka a ga-atụ site na “enwere m ike idughachi otu a na Premier League?’
rows.output: My progress this season has been so good that I can’t even imagine going back to the Premier League.
rows.reference: "Success for me at the moment will be gauged by 'can I return this club to the Premier League?'

rows.source: N’ihi nyiwe na ụlọ nke otu a, na enweghị mgbagha kwesịrị ịnọ na Premier League,” o kwuru.
rows.output: Due to the facilities and the club's home, I have no doubt that they should be in the Premier League," he said.
rows.reference: Because of the structure and facilities at this club, it undoubtedly belongs in the Premier League," he said.

rows.source: “Ọ bụghị ọrụ dị mfe iji laghachi ebe ahụ, mana enwere naanị ike ịhụta onwe m ka onye mere nke ọma ebe a ma ọ bụrụ na m nwere ike idughachi otu ahụ ebe ahụ.”
rows.output: "It's not an easy job to get back to that place, but I can only see myself as the person who did well there if I can bring that same team back there."
rows.reference: "It is not an easy task to get it there, but I would probably only view myself as being successful here if I can get the club back there."

rows.source: Ross nọ naanị afọ atọ n’ọrụ njikwa ya, ka obere oge gachara ka onye enyemaka na Dumbarton yana ọnụnọ ọnwa 15 n’otu ndị ọrụ Hearts.
rows.output: Ross was only three years into his management role, after a short stint as an assistant at Dumbarton and 15 months at Hearts.
rows.reference: Ross is only three years into his management career, after a period as assistant boss at Dumbarton and a 15-month spell on Hearts' coaching staff.

rows.source: Ọ gara nyere Alloa aka ịlaghachite na mgbatu ha gara n’ọkwa nke atọ, ma tụgharịa St Mirren site n’isi nke mgbatu gaa na mmeri iko Championship n’afọ asọmpi sotere.
rows.output: He helped Alloa return to the third division, and turned St Mirren from the bottom of the division to Championship cup winners in the following season.
rows.reference: He then helped Alloa recover from relegation to the third tier, and transformed St Mirren from the brink of relegation to Championship title winners the following season.

rows.source: Ma Ross kwuru na ọ nwere obi ume ala ugbu a karia ka ọ nwere n’oge onye egwu ya na Clyde, Hartlepool, Falkirk, St Mirren na Hamilton Academical.
rows.output: But Ross said he was now more relaxed than he had been during his time with Clyde, Hartlepool, Falkirk, St Mirren and Hamilton Academical.
rows.reference: And Ross says he feels more comfortable now than he ever did during his playing career at Clyde, Hartlepool, Falkirk, St Mirren and Hamilton Academical.

rows.source: “Ọ nwere ike ịbụ ezi njikọ,” ọ chetere, ịweghara ikike na Alloa.
rows.output: He might be a good connection, he thought, taking charge in Alloa.
rows.reference: "It was probably a real crossroads," he recalled, of taking charge of Alloa.

rows.source: “Ekwenyere n’ezie na njikwa bụ ihe ziri m nke ọma, karịa ịgba agba.
rows.output: I believe that management is something that I am good at, better than playing around.
rows.reference: "I genuinely did believe management was the right fit for me, more so than playing.

rows.source: Ọ dara ka ihe ọjọọ n’ihi na m mere nke ọma, ebiri ezigbo ndụ na ya, ma nwee ọhụụ ụfọdụ ihe ndị elu dị mma.
rows.output: It's better to be good because I did well, I had a good life with it, and I had some new experiences with good things.
rows.reference: It sounds bizarre because I did okay, made a reasonable living out of it, and enjoyed some reasonable highs.

rows.source: Mana ịgba agba na esi ike.
rows.output: But the ball is very hard.
rows.reference: But playing can be tough.

rows.source: Enwere ọtụtụ ihe ị ga-agafere kwa izu.
rows.output: There are many things you have to go through every week.
rows.reference: There are a lot of things you have to get through on a weekly basis.

rows.source: M ka na agafe nke ahụ n’okwu nke nsogbu na ndagide nke ọrụ ahụ mana njikwa dị mma n’anya.
rows.output: I have passed through that in the language of problems and the resistance of the work, but good management in the eye.
rows.reference: I still go through that in terms of the stresses and pressure of the job but management just feels right.

rows.source: Bido na mbụ achọrọ m ịme njikwa, ugbu a ana m eme ya, ọ kachasị enye m mmetụta obi ume ala, abụ m onwe m na ndụ okenye m niile.”
rows.output: First, I wanted to be in control, now I am, it's mostly given me a sense of peace, I am myself in my adult life."
rows.reference: I always wanted to manage and now I am doing it, it feels the most comfortable I have been in my own skin throughout my entire adult life."

rows.output: You can listen to the interview again on Sportsound on Sunday, September 30, on Radio Scotland at 12:00 and 13:00 BST

rows.output: The best time for a pint is 5:30 pm on Saturday, a study said.

rows.source: Okpomọkụ ọkọchị etipuola ego maka ụlọ mmanya ndị Britain ndị na aghọ ada mana dosakwuo nsogbu n’elu ndị azụmahịa ụlọ oriri na ọṅụṅụ.
rows.output: The high temperature has caused a shortage of ice for British-owned bars, which has led to problems for the owners of restaurants.
rows.reference: The summer heatwave has boosted takings for Britain's struggling pubs but heaped more pressure on restaurant chains.

rows.source: Otu ndị ụlọ mmanya hụrụ ka ahịa rịgoro pasentị 2.7 na Julaị - mana nrite n’ụlọ oriri na ọṅụṅụ dara pasentị 4.8, ọnụọgụ gosiri.
rows.output: The bars sector saw sales rise by 2.7% in July - but the restaurant sector's award fell by 4.8%, figures showed.
rows.reference: Pub and bar groups saw sales rise 2.7 per cent in July - but takings in restaurants were down 4.8 per cent, figures revealed.

rows.source: Peter Martin, nke ndị ndụmọdụ azụmahịa CGA, nke kpokọrọ ọnụọgụ ahụ, kwuru: “Anyanwụ ka dị yana nsonye England na World Cup toro ogologo ole atụrụ anya pụtara na Julaị sochiri otu usoro ka ọnwa nke Juun gara aga, mgbe ụlọ mmanya rịgoro pasentị 2.8, belụsọ na ndị ụlọ oriri na ọṅụṅụ nwere nnukwu nhịahụ.
rows.output: Peter Martin, from the CGA's business advisory arm, which compiled the figures, said: "The sun is still shining and England's World Cup participation has added to the long-term trend of rising pub sales, which increased by 2.8 percent in June, except for restaurants, which suffered a big drop."
rows.reference: Peter Martin, of business consultancy CGA, which compiled the figures, said: "Continued sunshine and England's longer than expected participation in the World Cup meant July followed a similar pattern to the previous month of June, when pubs were up 2.8 per cent, except that restaurants were hit even harder.

rows.source: Nrịda nke pasentị 1.8 n’azụmahịa ụlọ oriri na ọṅụṅụ na Juun kawanyere njọ na Julai.
rows.output: A decline of 1.8 percent in restaurant sales in June was followed by an even greater decline of 2.5 percent in July.
rows.reference: The fall of 1.8 per cent in restaurant trading in June just got worse in July.

rows.source: Ụlọ mmanya kachasị mee nke ọma otu yitere ihe dị ka otu ụlọ oriri na ọṅụṅụ si gbadaa.
rows.output: The best bar in the world is one that is more like a restaurant than a bar.
rows.reference: Drink-led pubs and bars performed by far the strongest with like-for-likes up more than restaurants were down.

rows.source: Ụlọ mmanya na ere nri tara ahụhụ n’anyanwụ, mana ọbụghị ka nke ndị na azụ ahịa ụlọ oriri na ọṅụṅụ.
rows.output: The bars and restaurants are crowded with people, but not as crowded as those in the hotels.

rows.output: The National Weather Service has issued a Storm Surge Watch for the Pinellas County coast, a Storm Surge Warning for the coastal areas of Hillsborough County, a Storm Surge Watch for the coastal areas of Manatee County, a Storm Surge Watch for the coastal areas of Sarasota County, a Storm Surge Watch for the coastal areas of Charlotte County, a Storm Surge Warning for the coastal areas of Lee County, and a Storm Surge Watch for the coastal areas of Collier County.
